data/story/intro_story.tres::awakening_l: ...Cold. Leaves in my mouth. Great start.
I reach for my name. Nothing. Not even the shape of one.
Two hands, one of them shaking. I'll start with the other one. ...And I'm not alone.
data/story/intro_story.tres::start.gate_: A cold draft rises from the dark. It smells of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town is on the other side. Go in?
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: Easy. Stay down. Hands like ice, pulse like a rabbit's. We'll fix that later.
Keep your voice low. We are not the only ones in these woods tonight.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: I don't know this place. I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: A friend. That's all I can give you, and it's already more than is safe.
Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand like you used to... never mind, just your hand.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: ...I feel them. All four, faintly. Like voices through a wall.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.re: Faint will do - it has to. Those torches on the ridge are looking for us.
Tell me: which Path resonates the strongest within you?
That one, then. Hold on to it, and it will hold on to you.
Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Someone there will be waiting for you.
Hear that? They're close. I'll draw them off the other way. They know my face; let them chase it.
So you go on alone. Don't thank me. Thank me when you're somewhere with a roof. Go!
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.wa: ...Gone, toward the torches. I never even asked their name.
data/story/intro_story.tres::prologue.se: The trees close up that way. The cave, then.
No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.
Whatever is waiting for me, it's through that cave.
Torches that way, cave this way. I'll take the one that isn't looking for me.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tutorial.wa: ...Hm. Woken. For this. Another of the little scavengers, I suppose.
...No. Not that. You smell familiar. Like old stone, and cold nights, in a house I used to keep.
The house does not open for just anyone. ...Show me.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Hollow: ...You smell familiar. Show me your hands.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Warden Stirs
At half health the Warden wakes a little more: a 1/1 Cave Echo rises beside it.
...You hit like someone I knew. Small. Stubborn.
A 1/1 Cave Echo rises beside the Warden.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tutorial.wa: ...Yes. The old walls do not lie. The spring at the end ran once. You would not remember.
Go. The house is yours to leave. Someone is waiting at the far end with a kettle on.
So. You're the one they sent through the old tunnel. Kettle's been on since noon.
I was told someone would come past the dry spring and that grumpy Warden. Nobody mentioned I'd need to wring them out.
This isn't trust, dearie. You could be anyone's spy, and whoever pushed you into that tunnel is reckless. I don't like reckless.
But a body in that state needs a bed, and I have far too much pie. Welcome to {town}. Questions later.
...I don't remember who I am. Not sure I'm worth the bed.
Hm. Then we start with tea and pie and work up from there.
First, get yourself known. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back and knock.
data/story/intro_story.tres::start.tunne: A narrow gap in the old treeline - easy to miss, easy enough to slip through, if you're not afraid of a shortcut.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.wake:: You wake in a forest clearing with leaves in your hair.
A faint glow of four colors fades from your hand, like a thought you almost had.
Beside you kneels someone hooded, very still, as if they have waited a long time.
data/story/intro_story.tres::equipment_v: Security Protocol One: assess the customer's gait. Adequate - you may approach at your current level of walking.
Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.
Everything on this rack is inventoried and oiled under Security Protocol Seven. Protocol Seven is need-to-know. You do not need to know.
Do not reach for the drawer. Its contents are classified, and so is your interest in them.
A return customer strengthens the economy and my employee-of-the-month case file. Please look satisfied for the record.
Fact: the beets came in early this year. The bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here.
Eat. Rest. Mind the questions you ask out loud, dearie. This town has ears.
And stop staring at my stick. Four little carvings in a ring, older than you, and none of your business.
You are warmer than you were. Don't mistake me, dearie, I am still watching you. The watching is free.
My pie recipe is pinned by the door, in my own hand. Round letters, careful loops. Copy it if you like. Smudge it and I will know.
Somebody in the square says you have a look of the old court about you. That is no prince, I told them. That is a damp young man with good posture.
And if you meet Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue. She'll be wrong.
I have told you the worst of me. The rest is easy, by comparison.
Go on, dearie, the next zone won't free itself. At my pace, we'd have to outlive the regime.
{prince}. I keep wanting to curtsy. My knees have voted against it.
Go on, the kingdom is waiting. The pie has less patience.
{prince}. {villain} let it slip to you, didn't he, that smug man. I had hoped to tell you myself.
Sit. When you are ready, the memories will come, and I will be here. With pie. Obviously.
Up and walking. Good. I am Elder Maren, dearie, and this is {town}, where the four Paths used to meet, and argue, and borrow each other's pans.
Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops.
Then {villain} took the Paths, one by one, and set his rulers over them. Every road out of town has a gatekeeper now: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.
Beat a gatekeeper and its road opens. Buy cards from Sable, fix your deck at the Deck Station, and come back to me for pie. Not answers. Pie.
The roads are waiting, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. One zone at a time.
You could still be anyone's spy. I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987.
Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.
The pie on the sill is cooling, dearie. Unlike you, it knows when to wait.
If you're looking for advice: eat something. If you're looking for more advice: eat something else.
I've given you all the answers you need for now, dearie. Further questions require fieldwork.
Mind the fountain, dearie. People throw wishes in it. Most of them are mine.
Off you go, dearie; I'll be here. I'm dependable at a speed you can barely measure.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.guard:: Hm. You came back. Wrote it in the notebook: 'came back.' Best two words I know.
Gate stays open. Always is. My girl's still up that road somewhere. In case.
Hm. That road. The Capital. You want to know why nobody comes back.
Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. {villain} chained all four.
So now it's Blackout, Famine, Restless Dead and Clutter up there. Dark streets, slow legs, no food that heals, rubbish in your deck.
You could walk in today. You would not walk far. Free the four zones: each one you free turns one service back on.
My girl Isla went up that road eight years ago. If you see her... tell her the gate is still open.
Hm. Services still broken. Count them on the board by the road.
Hm, each freed zone restores a service and makes the castle less frightening. My knees remain a local problem.
Hm. All four zones free. The lights are on up there. I can see them from here.
Go on. Knock on that castle door. Hard. And if you see Isla... I'm still watching the road.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.vendor: Well met, {wanderer}. Sable, darling: seller of cards, and of very good stories about cards.
You start with plain neutral cards. The Paths are where the power is. Browse, buy, then put it all to work at the Deck Station.
Where do my cards come from? The past. Next question. My prices are fair, mostly. {villain}'s taxes are not.
Back, darling? The cards are honest; the misprints simply have a more adventurous relationship with spelling.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.item_v: Hi! Hello! You look like you need supplies! Tilly Tonic! I'm teal today, which means the new batch works!
Everything here is one use in a fight! Equip what you buy on your Character screen, then use it on your turn!
Probably not on yourself! Unless it's a healing one! I tested the healing one! I'm fine! I'm green! I'm usually green!
Potions and charms, back for more! Equip them on your Character screen for fights - maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.l: The door rattles. Something behind it is muttering about a receipt.
Whatever it is, it is not open for business.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.b: OooOOOooo. Who disturbs the store room? We are VERY busy haunting it.
Ninety years ago the three of us bought one lantern between us. It never worked. Tilly's great-grandmother said: no receipt, no refund.
We waited, died, and kept waiting. Your haunting is very important to us.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.w: ...You're haunting a shop over a lantern.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.c: A FAULTY lantern. Four copper. With ninety years' interest, it is still four copper. We did the maths. We had time.
Nobody comes in until it is refunded. Or until somebody beats us at cards. Everyone settles everything with cards round here.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.a: ...Fine. FINE. You play like someone who kept the receipt.
We'll go. The chapel belfry has a lovely draught and nobody has complained about it in centuries.
Tell Tilly the lantern's on the top shelf, still broken after ninety years of nightly checks. We were thorough, if poorly lit.
Ha! No refund, no entry. Come back with a better deck. Or a receipt. Ideally both.
data/story/intro_story.tres::storeroom.c: Just shelves now. And one broken lantern on the top shelf, exactly where they said it would be.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.equipm: Halt. Equipment is issued on referral only. Security Protocol Two. Elder Maren does the referring.
Bring Elder Maren's blessing. Better posture is appreciated but cannot be accepted in its place.
data/story/intro_story.tres::quest.armor: Elder Maren sent you. I could tell from your gait. It says 'referred'. Congratulations: your file is now thick enough to be a file.
Before I issue gear, protocol asks for exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight. Any win counts. I will know.
Fact: things roam the edges of town. The outskirts, round the lanes. They are rude and they are close.
Beat one. Then come back and I will hand you something pointy.
One fight won. That is the whole requirement. So far I count zero. I am very good at counting to zero.
Security Protocol Four: check the outskirts. Enemies roam the edges of town. Any win counts.
I will be here, guarding the drawer.
One fight, won. Stamp. Stamp. Stamp. Three stamps is the correct number of stamps.
Security Protocol Twelve: report to Elder Maren. She decides where things get pointed.
Your Starter Blade. The first unit you play each battle hits a little harder. Do not run with it.
And all five equipment slots are yours now: helm, weapon, armor, boots, relic.
The good stuff is rarer, and you can only wear so much of it until you level up. Protocol. Fact: bears do not wear helms. Bears are wiser than us.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.hidden: You found the chest, so I suppose you've earned a look. Epic and Legendary goods, quiet prices.
{villain}'s tax collectors don't know this stall exists. Let's keep it that way. Shh.
A cellar hatch beside the old cottage, chained shut. Someone has scratched two little crossed swords into the wood.
Whatever is down there is not open for business. Yet.
Word around the square: the abandoned cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started roaring at night.
From the cellar. Somebody brave should check the hatch. Somebody like you.
WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION - ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! Mind the third stair; it bites without an introduction.
For a thousand years the four Paths settled their rivalries in the old arena, until {villain} chained the doors. SO WE DUG.
Since you freed a zone, THE RING IS OPEN! Battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, with prizes: ring-exclusive gear, gold, essence!
First clears pay out. Repeats are for GLORY. And for snacks. I brought snacks.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Announ: IN THIS CORNER: A CHALLENGER! IN THAT CORNER: ME! (normal voice) Hello.
THE SAND IS HOT AND THE CEILING IS LOW! Pick a fight, champion - the crowd is mostly my echo, and he agrees with EVERYTHING!
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.alchem: The door of Auntie Alembic's is bolted. A note is pinned to it in green ink, in what looks like four handwritings at once:
'CLOSED UNTIL TWO ZONES ARE FREE. {villain} TOOK MY CAULDRON. I AM BREWING IN THE SINK. THE SINK IS COPING. - A.'
With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}. Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring essence. Bring courage. Bring a fire blanket.
Auntie Alembic. Alchemist. Do not touch anything. ...Fine. Touch that one. It likes you.
Whenever you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, the extras turn into essence of that card's Path.
Bring me ALL the essence of two Paths, plus a little gold, and I will brew you a card of BOTH. Random. Unpredictable. Occasionally on fire.
They say there was one spring once, the Wellspring, that fed all four Paths. Everything mixed at the source, dear. That is the kingdom I brew for.
Essence of two Paths and a little gold, dear; faith helps with the waiting. Lower your voice around the red flask - it takes things personally.
You do not have enough essence of two different Paths yet. Collect more duplicates, then come back. The cauldron will wait.
The cauldron is patient. Please don't confuse patience with having had lunch.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.object: {villain} rules the four Paths through his rulers. Beat each road's gatekeeper, then free its zone by beating the boss of its main dungeon.
The imperial road to the Capital is open from the start, but its broken services will flatten you. Free the zones first. Gatekeeper Brannoch can explain.
All four Paths are free. Buy cards, test yourself in the Undercroft, and brew something dangerous at the Alchemist's.
Something under the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road is open for business. Listen for the crowd.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.alchem: Auntie Alembic's, the Alchemist, is now open in {town}. Bring your leftovers.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.pack_v: Psst... hear that crinkle? That's possibility, with excellent packaging.
Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods - packs only. Open one where the light's good; if I cry, I want to see what I'm crying about.
How it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. Lots of foil, no paperwork. The Necrocrats find it upsetting.
Free a zone and I stock its pack. Until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse! Sniff, if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.
Browse, sniff, but don't shake the packs. ...A little, then; I'm a collector, not a strong person.
A repeat customer... shh, listen to that foil. You understand me, and I don't know what to do with that.
Fenwick pulls a curtain aside. "The back room. Prismatic packs: every Path in one wrapper.
They only exist because the Paths are talking to each other again. Terrible for my exclusivity. Wonderful for my sales."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.vendor: Crinkle! You've made a wrapper very happy.
No refunds on bad luck. Bad luck is non-transferable.
It wants to be opened. I'm trying to respect its wishes without getting involved.
Gold, friend. The foil does not accept good intentions.
Not enough gold. The wrapper can tell.
Not yet. That one is still a rumour in a wrapper.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.tailor: Try everything on. The mirror is polite; I am not.
Hat! Hat. Marvellous head. Hold still: your left shoulder is a size braver than your right.
Pip Threadwell, Haberdasher and Hemmer! Everything in here is purely cosmetic. It will not make you stronger, braver or better at card games.
It will make you LOOK all three, which is eighty percent of the job. Try anything on in the little mirror first: hats up top, cloaks down the back, dye on both.
Free zones and climb levels, and I will find grander stock. I hear rumours of rarer pieces, too. People tell hatmakers everything.
Back to change your mind and your hat? Excellent - one of those I can fit properly.
My favourite head, in the nick of time! Brim, brooch or billowing - this could be a hem-ergency.
Oh, you have been busy. New fabrics arrived. Do not ask where from. Some of them were yelling.
Stock has grown! Freed zones send me their finest fashions. Slightly singed, mostly fabulous.
Between us: a crown made of living leaves is growing in a bin somewhere in the Verdant Dump. And a cloak that has survived more than you have is draped over a chest on a muscly island.
And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone has to defeat the person who owns it first.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.boug: Gorgeous. Truly. You are going to turn heads, mostly in confusion.
Wear it out! A hat cannot have an entrance if you keep it in a bag!
Sold! Such a dramatic fit - the hat looks surprised to be wearing you.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.poor: Gold, my dear head. Thread is not free, and neither is my charm.
A little more gold, my dear head. I can work wonders with fabric, but it insists on being paid for.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.lock: Not yet. That one is still on the sewing table, and it is sulking.
data/story/intro_story.tres::tailor.owne: You own that one already! Do introduce it to the outside world.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.hint.p: Stocked once the Gainlands' final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the Endless Buffet's final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the Verdant Dump's final dungeon is cleared.
Stocked once the D.N.A.'s final dungeon is cleared.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.hint.g: Fig can only get these once the Gainlands are free.
Fig can only get these once the Endless Buffet is free.
Fig can only get these once the Verdant Dump is free.
Fig can only get these once the D.N.A. is free.
The back crates open at level 10, or once two zones are free, whichever comes first.
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.card_v: Sable pats a stack of wrapped bundles. "Surprise packs, darling. Fresh from the crates, and I never ask a crate where it has been.
What's inside? The crate has declined to comment, darling, and I admire a professional."
Sable grins at you. "The back crates are open, darling - more cards, bigger surprises, the same discreet fainting policy."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.black_: Fig Sly taps a gold-edged wrapper. "Guaranteed good stuff. Do not ask where the guarantee comes from.
It is not legal. It is, however, very shiny."
data/story/intro_story.tres::pack.reward: The Path sends you its pack: %s.
Where every champion starts: loud, dusty and mostly forgiving.
The crowd has stopped laughing and started betting.
Only legends stand here. Only the sand remembers who fell.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: Warm-Up Brawl
A rookie gladiator rattles inside oversized armor. Bring your own deck; the armor has enough room for its own audience.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel.
Lethal Lunch
The lunch rush has an enemy blocker, ten HP and no mercy. You have exactly one turn and just enough energy.
PUZZLE: win THIS turn. Preset board. If the turn ends and your opponent still stands, you lose.
The Neutral Mile
The Marshal's favorite warm-down: no Paths, no tricks, no excuses. Everyone fights with a borrowed gladiator's kit.
RESTRICTED DECK: you fight with the Gladiator's Kit (neutral cards), not your own deck.
Hold the Line
A stampeding squad charges across the sand before you can even take a breath. You only have to outlast them.
PUZZLE: survive 3 of the enemy's turns. Preset board; the enemy moves first. You win when the third enemy turn ends and you still stand.
Spells Only, Please
The Cardboard Colossus does not like being hit by anything with a heartbeat. Win without playing a single unit.
RESTRICTED DECK + RULE: you fight with the Spellslinger's Satchel and may NOT play unit cards this duel.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Getting Soggy
At half health the Colossus gets soggy: its units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
THE COLOSSUS IS... DAMP! (normal voice) Someone left the mop bucket out again.
The Colossus is soggy: its units get -1/-0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: The Four Fists
A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a hand on every card. Bring your best deck.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Fourth Fist
At half health the Champion uses its fourth fist: its units get +1/+0 for the rest of the fight.
THE CHAMPION RAISES ITS FOURTH FIST! (normal voice) Nobody knows where it keeps it.
The Champion's units get +1/+0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.arena: Zero to Hero
The Wall of Fame has two blockers and eleven HP. The crowd has already booked your funeral. Show them lethal.
PUZZLE: win THIS turn. Preset board, five energy, two blockers to deal with.
The Marshal
Announcer Grand Bellows steps onto the sand. He has not lost a bout in eleven years. He is smiling, and so is the moustache.
Your own deck, full HP. Win the duel. No excuses.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: THE CROWD GOES WILD
On his 3rd turn the crowd joins in: a 1/1 Rowdy Fan climbs into the ring.
Next turn: a fan climbs into the ring.
THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Please stay behind the rope. There is a rope.
A 1/1 Rowdy Fan climbs into the ring.
INTERMISSION
At half health Bellows calls an intermission: he heals 2, and his units sit down through his next turn.
INTERMISSION! (normal voice) I'm having soup. THE SOUP IS WINNING.
Bellows heals 2; his units sit out his next turn.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.scree: The gates are chained until the first zone is free.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.won.f: VICTORY ON THE SAND - THE PRIZE IS YOURS! The echo would like it known that it believed in you first.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.won.r: Another win for the books. The crowd roars (and tosses you some coins).
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.lost:: NOT THIS TIME, CHAMPION! Come back whenever you're ready; the sand has yet to win a rematch.
data/story/intro_story.tres::arena.puzzl: PUZZLE SOLVED - THE CROWD GOES WILD! A triumph for thinking, shouted at full volume!
The puzzle got the better of you. Study the board and try again.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.subt: Rips while-you-wait. Tips accepted in protein.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.here: You are here. A Rip is stationed here.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.lock: No station yet. Walk into the town there and a cousin will wake up and rip one into the wall.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.warn: Ripping out of a zone ends your visit: you arrive at full HP, and the roaming enemies there come back. Rips are free. Beefcakes charge for spotting, and spotting is also free.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.oper: Rip Tearson (Cousin #4, the One Who Eats)
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.stat: The home station. A well-supported sky is a happy sky.
The elevator lobby. A cousin ripped it into the wall beside the Out-Of-Order sign. It is the only thing in the building that works.
Between the hot tub and the protein stand, where the gains are public.
The Endless Buffet: The Grand Pantry
A short walk from the heavy meal table. The cousin ripped it open just by the napkins.
The Verdant Dump: The Compost Grange
Right by the harvest table. The Rip is slightly damp. So is everything.
A rip into the hideout under the Capital. Do not ask how we found it. We followed the smell of Fig Sly's hot sauce through the fabric of space.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: HNNNGH. SPOTTER! Spot me! No, not you, the other guy. ...Hello. Welcome to the Beefcake Rift Express.
We tear the world open so you don't have to walk, buddy. Two men hold the sky - that's our overhead.
The sky is surprisingly heavy. Do NOT skip sky day. And do not look at the seam. It is not a seam. It is a PUMP.
Reach a town and we send a cousin to rip a station there. All named Rip; around cousin four, naming became a cooldown exercise.
Walk into a town, and its station wakes up. Then you can rip between any two of them. Thank you for ripping with the Express.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.retu: Back for another rip, little buddy? Say where, and we will tear it right open. Rips are free.
Spotting is free, buddy. Hydration is a bring-your-own-water situation.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: HNNNGH... Rip Tearson, Beefcake Rift Express, serving this exact spot. I'm a cousin; we hire entirely on relative strength.
We are all very proud of one another and rarely speak.
Say where, buddy. We will rip it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.retu: Need a rip, brother? I've held this sky since breakfast, and I'd hate to put it down with no one through it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.intr: Shhh. Keep it down, there is a Wrinkle sleeping behind the crates. Rip Tearson, Cousin #7, Rift Express. Allegedly.
I was told this place did not exist, so I ripped a hole to it. Sometimes you just have to want it. And the sauce smell helped.
Grab the edges! On three! One!
Hold the sky, brother! Feel the burn! RRRRRIP!
Spot this whole dimension, brother! Lift with your LEGS - lower back does not mean lower universe!
Loosen the shoulders. Roll the neck. Tear a hole in the fabric of space. And never, ever skip leg day.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.arri: The rift folds shut behind you with a very satisfied pop. A nearby Beefcake flexes at the hole to say well done.
The rift drops you by the lobby elevator and pops shut. You catch a fluttering memo: YOU WERE NOT AUTHORIZED TO ARRIVE.
You check for an approved way to have arrived. The memo offers none.
The rift spits you out next to the Swole Station. A passing brute gives you a thumbs-up, then another to himself, then one to the hole.
You land in the Pantry and receive a napkin before you find your balance. Priorities are immaculate.
You arrive at the Grange in a whiff of ozone, mulch and gym sock. The Express leaves a personal impression.
The rift spits you out in the Crease. Somebody says shh. Somebody else says it was not them. The rift closes politely.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.unlo: A Beefcake cousin has ripped a Rift Station into this town. Fast travel unlocked.
Rift Station unlocked: the Department of Necrotic Affairs. A cousin ripped it in beside the Out-Of-Order sign. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Gainlands. Two cousins have ripped it in with their bare hands and are now doing a victory pose. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Endless Buffet. A cousin ripped it in, then asked if there were seconds. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Verdant Dump. A cousin ripped it in, then looked at his hands, then at the hole, then at his hands again. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
Rift Station unlocked: the Crease, the hideout under the Capital. A very quiet cousin ripped it in. Fast travel to and from here is now open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::travel.sign: Rips while-you-wait. Space torn to order. No refunds on the sky.

What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.

data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.beefca: You did it. Grandmaster Flex is out. He made me stretch for forty minutes. I cried twice. Good tears.
The bridge stays down now, but I still oil the crank every morning. Maintenance is how I say sorry.
Want to spar? Gently. I'll spot you. I'm a spotter. ...I'm SO glad I can say that quietly.

The planks thump down across the gorge. The Gainlands are open.

data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.bre: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. I'm Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes power the kingdom on mills and hamster wheels, and move folks by throw and by portal.
Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge. Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight. Every... every plate.
We haven't crumbled. Tired, mind. If you fall, I catch you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two: never skip leg day. Rule three... I forget. Two is plenty.
Back for more? Good. The only bad rep is the one nobody spotted.
Beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes. The illegal flavour... ah, that's the one worth remembering.
The old king used to come up for the Lifting Festival every summer, with his boy. Little fella tried my dumbbell and sat down hard on his royal behind.
Laughed about it, too. Four colours in his hands, plain as day. You've got a look about you... never mind. Old man talk. Where was I.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.gus: Foreman Gus: wheels turning, grid humming, hamsters... *volunteers*... fed. Pre-workout's in the water, but so far I'm only feeling the water.
The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels go to a hundred. The extra ten is me, crying quietly.
They want the same out of the city wheels up in the Capital. Those crews get told it's cardio. It isn't.
Grid still humming? If it goes quiet, somebody's resting, and the regime writes that down as a personal insult.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.ton: LET'S GO! NEW RECRUIT! Coach Brutus Benchley! Retired champion, current motivator, part-time merchant! Protein, powder, pasteboard! Supplements for your DECK!
REGIME-APPROVED MERCHANDISE! Not actually approved, but these old cards have a GREAT ATTITUDE!
*whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter. Nothing under it... just iron, which officially isn't anything.
LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are pumped and my whistle has been SAVING ITS BREATH!
*whispering* Nobody's mentioned the floorboard. I'd like to keep our relationship on that footing.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.qui: Aha, a student! Professor Pump, Beefcake scholar, lecturing from this very log. I have written seventeen books.
Fifteen concern biceps; the regime burned the other two, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Four questions on the Beefcakes, their energy and their transport. Every answer is on a sign, a poster or a Beefcake's lips somewhere in the Gainlands.
Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. Today, we train the brain-ceps.
Back for another set of questions? Splendid - knowledge gains are retained even when you stop flexing.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quiz.re: Zero, with no reward this time. A clean baseline; research begins somewhere.
Consult the signs before your next attempt. Your eyes may do the heavy reading.
One. A muscle twitch of knowledge. Take this pat on the back. It's a small one.
Two. Half-credit, graded on a bicep curve. In the Gainlands half a rep still counts. Just not for much.
Three! One shy of a clean sweep. Take your reward and flex responsibly.
FOUR! A perfect set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gainer, Class A. The reward is real. The certificate is imaginary.
Another lap! The Gainlands pay a small processing fee for repeat attendance.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::quiz.no: Not a pass yet; read the signs around the Gainlands and return. We are training recall, not regret.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::npc.min: *cue synthesizer* Welcome, welcome, WELCOME to PUMP IT UP PAST MIDNIGHT! I'm your host, Chet Thunderabs, and it is 3 A.M. somewhere, which is where I live!
You've seen the late-night tapes! 'Feel the burn!' But WAIT, there's MORE! My assistant is a legwarmer. My producer is ALSO a legwarmer.
The regime banned my show for 'unauthorized fun'! These cameras are STILL ROLLING - you can't spell resistance without... well, SPANDEX HELPS!
Today's show: REP COUNTER! Eight reps, one beat. Hit the beat and I give you a shiny medallion of pure encouragement!
Rewards for performance, plus a one-time bonus on your very first set! Three easy payments of gold? NO! FREE! Operators are standing by! And one, and two...
Back again! My fans! Both of you! Hear that? That's the sound of Spandex, applauding.
Remember: the beat is your friend. The beat does not judge. The beat is judging, but quietly.
data/story/gainlands_story.tres::reps.in: Eight reps. Watch the ring: press SPACE (or click) the moment it closes on the bar. Perfect, Good, OK or Miss.

At half health Fennel force-feeds you a biscuit (you heal 2) and a 1/1 Snack joins his side.
TASTE IT. It is for the war effort. The BISCUIT is for the war effort.
You heal 2. A 1/1 Snack joins Fennel.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gourmand_np: The simmer let go. The sauce let go. Plain bread. No sauce. I could weep. I am weeping.
The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own sauces. The real one ALWAYS tasted. Same face. Ask yourself who was wearing the apron.
The Test Kitchen is at the far end of the Buffet, and it was never making casserole. Take a biscuit. Take two. Heroes need carbs.
The pantry door stays shut until you learn to cook. Consider this a closed-course meal.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::ZONE_M: Key Ingredients
The great pantry door is locked and the chef with the key is extremely seasoned. Win the key and find out what the Grand Chef is really cooking.
Win the pantry key from Chef Fennel Gravois
The great pantry door at the end of the orchard lane
Step through the pantry door into the Endless Buffet
The open pantry door on the orchard lane
Help the kitchen: finish a favour in the Endless Buffet
Basil, Sous-Chef Tarragon or Madame Mirepoix
Shut down the Test Kitchen
The Test Kitchen, at the far end of the halls
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::hud.obje: The Endless Buffet: the Grand Pantry is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down for a hearty meal, or walk back down to town. Everything here looks wonderful.
Something under the Test Kitchen smells wrong.
Three courses in a row. Your HP carries from one course to the next and nothing heals in between. Finish all three for a unique Gourmand card.
You already took the unique card from this freezer. You can still eat your way through the courses for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, sentinels and meatballs (prototype batch, unfortunately) will be back next time. The buffet, as the name suggests, is endless.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.main_: The Test Kitchen sits at the far end of the table: a gleaming glass-and-steel laboratory with a very large, very unfinished cannon sticking out of the roof. A banner reads INNOVATION SEASON.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.heal_: You sit down to a hearty meal: roast something, a bowl of soup the size of a bathtub, and a roll that hugs you back. HP restored.
Your HP is full, and the chef says there are no seconds. You both know this is a serving of fiction.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.hit::: BONK! A runaway prototype meatball hits you right in the shins. (-2 HP)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.wake:: You wake up face-down in a bowl of mashed potatoes at the Grand Pantry. Basil is holding a ladle and a very long receipt.
"You fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's a fishing fee... sorry, sorry, I don't set the catch of the day.
Don't tell the taste testers. If anyone asks, say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.chest: A hidden stash! Nobody tasted that one. Lettuce rejoice.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.lande: You stick the landing. Peeling yourself off it takes longer.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.soup_: You fell in the gravy! Somebody fishes you out and sets you on dry ground. (-1 HP)
Fell into the soup at %s - fished out at the last safe spot, 1 damage to zone HP.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.gate_: The golem steps aside. The way is open.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.picku: You already took the one lying here. Come back on your next visit; the pantry restocks overnight.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.oven_: Ding! A Hearty Pot Pie, golden and steaming, drops into your bag. The oven looks very proud of itself.
The Grand Oven rumbles. "A pie needs honey, basil and a ghost pepper. I am an oven, not a miracle."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.taste: Smooth, balanced, a touch of citrus. You nod like a professional. +HP.
You take a sip and blink through a tear. Five stars would feel stingy - big recovery!
Your palate sharpens. You can taste what the cheese had for breakfast. A little extra HP for the visit.
The judges are impressed and tip you for the privilege of watching. +gold.
You find the ghost pepper in spoon three. Your ears ring in protest. -1 HP.
You taste boiled water with a hint of ambition. The judges study their shoes; nothing else happens.
You need 8 gold for the taste test. The station declines to sample your good intentions.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.fount: You ladle some soup. Tomato with a hint of basil. Warm all the way down. +HP.
You take a second ladle of cream of mushroom. The fungus has a rich inner life. +HP.
Third ladle: minestrone, mostly noodles. You feel taller. +HP.
You ladle some soup. Delicious, but you are already stuffed to the brim.
The fountain's tank is dry for now. It refills on your next visit. Soup takes time.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.cooki: The dispenser wants 5 gold. Fortune favours the people who bring change.
You crack the cookie open. A tiny paper slip falls out. It reads:
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::fx.mend_: Old Meatloaf is mended! He gets up, stretches, and sizzles a little.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.ing: Brisket nods slowly. "Go on in. Mind the cheese.
The cheese takes trespassing personally. You're walking on its rind."
Brisket sniffs the air, and his eyes close in bliss. "Saffron. Real saffron.
Do you know how long it has been?" He takes the threads with great tenderness and steps aside.
"Go on through. Tell the Cheddar Cliffs they are overdue for a good grating. Yes, Chef."
Brisket does not look at you. He looks over your head, at the horizon. "This gate opens for one pinch of saffron.
Real saffron. It grows in the Candy Field. Ask a sous-chef if you are lost."
He sighs at you. "Bring saffron from the Candy Field; this gate has a very particular taste in visitors."
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.que: Sir Loin raises his fork in salute. "You mended Old Meatloaf, so you are a friend of the Pantry. The town is yours."
Sir Loin inspects you. "Old Meatloaf walks again. Basil sends thanks, and orders, which are: let you in. Yes, Chef!"
He lowers his fork-lance. The gate swings open.
Sir Loin clanks to attention. "HALT! Nobody enters Layer-Cake Town until Old Meatloaf has been mended.
That is Basil's request. Speak to Basil in the Grand Pantry. Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::gate.bat: Colonel Casserole tips his lid. "A fair fight, well fought. The Pancake Plateau is open to you. Mind the syrup; it pools."
Colonel Casserole bubbles ominously. "Halt! This gate is guarded by a Colonel.
No passes, no bribes - challenge me to single combat with cards. I shall defend this gate to the last course."
"If you win, you pass. If you lose, you do the washing up. Both are honourable."
Defeat Colonel Casserole in a card battle to open the way to the Pancake Plateau. Your HP carries over as usual.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hub: Hub of the Endless Buffet. The Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it.
Nobody leaves hungry. (Innovation Season is now in effect. Sample participation is mandatory.)
- Innovation: please do not ask about the Special Sauce
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.exi: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet and surrender your sample; we just mopped.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hea: Sit. Eat. Do not ask what the gravy is made of.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ven: Cards and cakes, mostly cards. Reservations recommended; table manners apply even to your deck.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ove: Honey, basil and one ghost pepper make one Hearty Pot Pie.
Do not open the oven to check on the pie. It is already working under considerable heat.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.fou: Three ladles per customer. The soup of the day is soup.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gol: We are the Gourmands: chefs of the kingdom.
We feed the kingdom. We protect the kingdom.
We cook food golems to guard it. They answer every order with "Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.coo: Each one holds a hint about a secret. Handle with care. The secrets are crumbly.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.old: Out of order. Needs sea salt and a black truffle. Please be gentle.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.for: Please do not eat the trees.
The trees say the same about you.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.qui: Professor Pate asks 4 questions on the Gourmands and their kitchens. The answers are on the signs of the Endless Buffet.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tru: A black truffle was last seen near this tree.
The tree was last seen near the truffle. They are inseparable.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.can: Everything here is edible. Not everything is wise.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.stu: Now taping: three tickets, one stove, zero patience.
Live studio audience: a bowl of sprouts. Please applaud; they cannot.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: Judges: a spoon, a larger spoon and a very patient cloche.
Results may vary. Please distinguish applause from your stomach making a statement.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.sal: A pinch here. A pinch there. A pinch of sea salt for your troubles.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.but: Step on the jelly pad. Mind the ceiling.
(There is no ceiling. Mind the sky.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.pad: 3. There is no step 3. There is only boing.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.riv: Thick, hot and entirely made of gravy.
The only ways across: a crouton raft or the lazy susan.
Do not swim. Do not wade. Do not ask how deep it is.
If you fall in, somebody will fish you out. It costs 1 HP.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.raf: Hop on when it docks. Ride. Hop off on the other side.
Keep arms and legs inside the croutons. Passengers are not part of the garnish.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.sus: The world's largest serving platter, slowly turning.
Step on at one side. Step off at the other. Patience is a garnish.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.raf: Eastbound and northbound. Please have exact change.
(There is no change. It is gravy. Everything is gravy.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ban: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gat: Admission: a letter from Basil, proving Old Meatloaf has been mended.
Admission: defeat the Colonel in a card battle.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.che: Sharp cheese ahead. Do not lean on or lick the walls; we cannot keep putting this delicately.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.cak: Please do not bite the buildings. They are load-bearing cake.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.pan: Syrup flows downhill. So do tourists.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.min: Please do not lock yourself in. (Somebody already has.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.mai: Please do not ask what the cannon is for. The cannon is for dinner.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ins: Found: a lab where there was a kitchen, a cannon where there was a stove, and a Grand Chef who never tastes anything.
Back at lunch. If I am not back, check the compost.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ste: Four ingredients, in the right order, tastes like victory.
Read the recipe card. Vibes are not one of the four ingredients.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.gol: Golems stand guard. Golems ask nicely, once.
Golems answer every order with "Yes, Chef!"
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.cak: Nobody leaves hungry. Nobody leaves without a slice, either.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.che: Cheese. More cheese. Something to put on the cheese. Different cheese.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.lo: You face a wardrobe-sized prototype meatloaf in a ketchup glaze. Its frown suggests it would like a second draft.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.je: A lime gelatin sentinel with a spoon spear and a fruit cocktail soul. Prototype Mk. 2.
You watch it wobble through a thought. Management has discouraged these.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.me: Pure momentum with a side of sauce. A failed prototype that escaped. Nobody knows what it is running from. It is probably the cannon.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::enemy.ca: A pot-bellied colonel with a lid for a hat and a ladle for a sword. Thirty years of service, forty years of cheese.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.odal: Psst. Hello. I'm Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it. Every plate is a promise. Every golem is a guard.
Ten years ago {villain}'s people came to the Buffet, and the Grand Chef... changed. Chef ALWAYS tastes, and this Chef doesn't. She just smiles at the soup.
She put the Special Sauce in every pot. Our rules: nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. Nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.
You came back... good, good. A Gourmand never stops stirring, so technically this panic is a cooking method.
What do we say? "Yes, Chef" - on the lowest possible heat.
The Grand Chef has very good hearing, for someone who never tastes a thing.
The real Chef baked a birthday cake for the little prince once. Four layers, one for each Path. He licked the frosting off all four and left the rest.
Chef laughed for a week. Last month I mentioned that cake to her, and she didn't remember it. Chef remembers every cake she's ever baked.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.tarr: Sous-Chef Tarragon, fetcher of things - oh, good, more hands! I've been running all day and still haven't caught up with lunch.
We're always out of something. Honey, basil, ghost pepper... half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen, and nothing comes back. I once fetched a whole pig. Wrong pig. It's still angry.
Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. She hears everything. She just never tastes anything.
Ingredients, please, anything? I'm one leaf away from calling this a salad and going home.
I'm hungry and a bit scared. If either came with a side dish, we'd be sorted.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.dolc: Madame Mirepoix. Dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu: three cards, lightly foiled, served with disdain.
Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. The stamp is on the decorative cake, which has never looked more unappetizing.
I take gold, favours and sprinkles, in that order. I do not take the Special Sauce. I have been pretending to eat it for months.
Your cards are plated, darling; the cake is decorative. As for the Special Sauce, I recommend the air beside it.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river, honey up the Butte
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Pantry Run
The Grand Pantry is out of everything that matters. Sous-Chef Tarragon needs three ingredients from around the Buffet. Lettuce not panic.
Gather ingredients around the Buffet
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: You can fetch? Wonderful! We need three ingredients, quick. Our stolen deliveries are scattered all over the Buffet: truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river, honey up the Butte.
Pick up any three and come back. I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron.
Bring any three ingredients from around the Buffet. The pantry is empty, and I can't keep calling that a minimalist menu.
Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved! For today!
Here, a little something. It's a card. It's soup. It's soup you can play.
The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. Fetching has a wonderful sense of repetition; I'd like to send it back.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The Grand Oven, by the arch
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Bake Me a Pie
Madame Mirepoix wants a Hearty Pot Pie, baked fresh in the Grand Oven from honey, basil and a ghost pepper, and delivered to her counter.
Bake a Hearty Pot Pie in the Grand Oven
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: A favour, darling. A customer of mine wants a Hearty Pot Pie, a real one, and the Grand Oven is sulking. It keeps being asked to cook prototypes.
Bake one for me: honey, giant basil and a ghost pepper, into the Grand Oven by the arch, then bring it here. Careful with the pepper. It is not a team player.
One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have cake.
A pie. A real one, golden and warm. My customer is going to cry.
I am going to cry. Discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing. Thank you.
The best pie this Pantry has seen in years. The oven would like a word with you. I believe it wants to say thank you.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Old Meatloaf, by the west wall of the Grand Pantry
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Mend the Meatloaf
Old Meatloaf, the Grand Pantry's oldest golem, has stopped working. Basil thinks sea salt and a black truffle will get him back on his loaf.
Mend Old Meatloaf with sea salt and a black truffle
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quest.bu: Um. A word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts. We got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.
He needs sea salt for his joints and a black truffle for his heart, both out in the Buffet. Mend him and Sir Loin will let you through the Layer-Cake Town gate. Yes, Chef? ...Please?
Old Meatloaf is over by the west wall of the Grand Pantry. Sea salt, a black truffle, and a bit of tenderness.
He's walking! He's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying. I'm standing near onions.
Here's your reward, and Sir Loin will open his gate for you now. Well done. Yes, Chef.
Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others. They know.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.old_: Old Meatloaf is slumped on the floor, in two pieces, with crossed-out eyes. A note on his chest reads: SEA SALT AND A BLACK TRUFFLE. PLEASE BE GENTLE.
You season Old Meatloaf's joints with the sea salt and tuck the black truffle where his heart should be. He sits up slowly.
"...Chef?" he says. "Yes, Chef," you say, because it feels right. His eyes uncross.
Old Meatloaf stands guard with great dignity. "Yes, Chef!" he whispers.
He says it to you. You are not a chef. He does not mind.
He is just glad nobody wants to turn him into a cannon.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.quiz: Professor Pate, Keeper of the Cookbook. I've read every recipe twice; the footnotes have an excellent finish.
I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce. I looked. I even licked the index.
Four questions about the Gourmands: who they are, what they cook, how their golems speak. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Endless Buffet.
Answer well and earn gold, glory and the respect of a very old book. Answer poorly and earn a gentle, scholarly sigh, lightly salted.
Back to improve your score? Splendid. Knowledge, like a good roux, wants patience. And butter. Mostly butter.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.res: Zero, so no reward this time. We have established that knowledge does not rise on its own.
Read the signs and let the facts simmer. You cannot rush a well-seasoned answer.
One. A pinch of knowledge, barely seasoned. Here is a small token. It is a thimble of encouragement.
Two. Half-baked. A fine place to start. Half-baked things can still be rescued.
Three! Nearly perfect. Perfect would make me suspicious. Take your reward and a warm roll.
FOUR! A perfectly risen set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gourmand, First Class.
The reward is real. The certificate is imaginary.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.rep: Another round! The Cookbook pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::quiz.not: Not a pass. Wrong, but deliciously wrong. Walk the Endless Buffet, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.mini: *brass fanfare* CHEF FLAMBE FONTAINE, LIVE FROM THE CANDY FIELD: DINNER IN A DASH! The Test Kitchen cancelled us, so this is a SECRET BROADCAST!
Seven seasons on tape, and people STILL do my WHOOSH! Please rewind; the dramatic entrance is at the beginning.
My arch-rival, Chef Savannah Souffle, stole my Spaghetti Surprise. The surprise was more spaghetti. She took a job at the Test Kitchen. I wish her well, very far away.
Tonight's show: ORDER UP! Six tickets, one counter, no mercy. Stack each dish in the right order before the timer dings. Rewards for performance, and a first-time bonus!
My Turbo Tots toys were recalled. Not for safety: for spinning too well. Tonight's audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche. Let's COOK!
Back for another shift, champ? The cameras are always rolling. They are not. They ran out of film in two-thousand-three. Smile anyway.
Remember: the ticket is your friend. The ticket does not judge. The ticket is judging, but kindly.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.in: Six tickets. Press the ingredient stations in the right order (click or keys 1-6) before the timer runs out. A wrong ingredient tosses the plate and costs time. Faster is better.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.sh: Second ticket, and I do mean it!
Burger and fries, hot hot hot!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.wi: ORDER UP - THAT COUNTER IS BEAUTIFUL! You cook like someone who knows exactly where the camera is!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.fi: Your very first shift on the show! Here is your bonus, free, no obligation. It is a scroll.
Chef Savannah would call it Scroll Deluxe. She could put a garnish on the envelope and call it a course.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::order.lo: Not quite, chef - breathe! Even a souffle gets a second rise in my kitchen!
Re-tie your apron and try again! Those tickets can wait; this is a cooking show, not a farewell episode!
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.i: A huge pot bubbles on a fire. Beside it hangs the recipe card: seven clues for the Mystery Stew. Choose four of the six ingredients and add them in the right order.
Serve it when you are sure; the pot only tells you right or wrong.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.c: Exactly one of the Pumpkin and the Mushroom goes in the stew.
The Carrot has been banned from the stew. Long story.
The first ingredient is the Onion or the Carrot.
The Leek goes in after the Mushroom (not necessarily right after).
The Mushroom does not go in first.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.h: Start with what is banned and what must be present. Four of the six are in, two are out. Then place them one clue at a time.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.s: The stew thickens. The ladle hums. A small, heavy parcel rises out of the steam: the pot has given you its seasoning.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.a: The stew sits perfectly seasoned. Nothing left to cook.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.i: The pot needs exactly four different ingredients before you can serve it.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::recipe.w: The golem that tastes it gags politely. "Chef, this is not it."
You watch the stew go bland. The pot sighs like a recipe being ignored.
A single sad bubble rises. It pops. That was all it had to say.
A stash lies in the shade of the broccoli, in a loaf that has gone hollow.
On the Butte, behind the butter, someone left a present for the brave.
Candy is sweeter when it is hidden. Try the big jar in the south-east.
Between the shakers on the salt flats, something shines.
Cheddar tastes sharper from above. Take the lime jelly to the top.
Behind a wheel of cheese, a smaller wheel of gold.
At the summit of the pancakes, a tip: the syrup hides a treasure.
In Layer-Cake Town, behind a cake: a cake of another kind.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.inn: By order of the Grand Chef, under the seal of Colonel Crumb, Culinary Defense: every kitchen contributes to Prototype Development, for the war effort.
Taste-tester shifts are mandatory. Complaints will be seasoned and served.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.spe: Delicious. Compulsory. Do not ask what is in it.
It is in everything now. Please enjoy.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: Join the elite food-safety force. Free uniform, free meals, no questions.
(Previous taste testers are available for questions. They are not answering.)
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::effect.b: Nobody leaves hungry, least of all the Gourmands. Full bellies make for strong golems.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::effect.d: The Gourmands insist on formal dining; Refusemancers arrive dressed for the work that grew the dinner.
Test kitchens, food labs and an enormous, unfinished cannon. Somewhere inside, the Grand Chef is not the Grand Chef. HP carries in from the zone; only the canteen heals. Beat the boss to free the Buffet.
The Test Kitchen is quiet now, and the real Grand Chef is cooking. You can still run the prototypes for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except at the canteen.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Just measuring. Mind you, the Chef's soups add years to people. Bad for business. Good for everybody else. Heh.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Colone: Halt, traveller. This gate opens for a duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Honour Duel

En garde, traveller. A duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
Casserole's units get +1/+1.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-MIREPOIX.barks::0: This deck is underdressed, darling. A little butter. A little foil. Voila.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-MIREPOIX.barks::1: Decorative cake, darling. Please admire it without cutlery.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PATE.barks::0: A good answer is like a roux: patience, then butter. Mostly butter.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PATE.barks::1: Chalk again. Notes of limestone. Excellent body, no business being in my mouth.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLAMBE.barks::0: ORDER UP! Sixty seconds and a dream! WHOOSH! Mostly the dream!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FLAMBE.barks::1: Savannah Souffle calls that plating? WHOOSH! That's the sound of me declining to comment!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BASIL.barks::0: Chef ALWAYS tastes. Always. That's how you know it's Chef.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BASIL.barks::1: I'm brave. I'm brave. ...Have you seen my thyme? I'm running out of it.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ESCOFFINA.barks: Have you eaten? Sit. Eat. Then save the kingdom. In that order.
A full table is a safe table. Pull up a chair. That is an order.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-DOPPEL.barks::0: I tasted my soup today. As me. Too salty. It was mine.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-DOPPEL.barks::1: Third-class apprentice. Many dishes. I am trying. The dishes are also trying.

Find a hidden stash in the Buffet
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Over here. Quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.
The card is in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. Golden. You'll know it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited. I think. It feels a lot like the other thing.
The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The conveyor never stops, like the Eternal Queue it was modelled on. Each plate comes with a numbered ticket, stamped.
The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. 'Omakase.'
Behind him, a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Omakase
On his 4th turn the Itamae serves you a course, as the custom is: you heal 2.
Next turn: the Itamae serves the next course.
Omakase.
The Itamae serves you: you heal 2.
...Enough.
Near the end the Itamae sets down his knife: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
...Enough.
The Itamae's units get -1/-0.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. 'Omakase,' he says. This time it sounds like thank you.
A sign over the dock doors reads TASTE-TESTER ENTRANCE. Beneath it, in smaller letters: NO EXIT.
The air smells of caramel and solder. Somewhere deep inside, a cannon coughs and a dozen chefs say "Yes, Chef!" very quietly.
The Loading Dock
You pass incoming ingredient crates and outgoing unlabelled ones. Research appears to be a one-way conversation.
Ingredient Intake
A corrupted sous-chef guards the conveyor belt. Everything on the belt is a little too shiny.
The Taste Panel
You face a silent panel of grim judges. They taste your dishes as though flavour might be used against them.
Cold Storage Prototypes
Frozen failures line the walls. Some of them are still moving. One of the freezers is humming louder than the rest.
The Staff Canteen
A hot meal, an honest one. The only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.
The Food Construct
An experimental food construct, stitched together from three kinds of meat and one regret. (Elite)
The Cannon Bay
The unfinished war machine looms. It is enormous, held together by gravy and willpower.
The Armory Pantry
You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons. Take what you can carry; someone has overthought serving suggestions.
The Special Sauce Vats
Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. This is where the corruption is made.
The Mk. IX Prototype
You face the Test Kitchen's finest unfinished war machine: armed, hungry and still awaiting seasoning. (Elite)
The Whistleblower
A sous-chef hiding in the dry goods wants to tell you something about the Grand Chef.
The cook behind the counter whispers: "The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own soup ten years ago. Nobody noticed. Everybody noticed. Nobody said."
You pour a vat out. Behind it, a service door opens on the Executive Test Kitchen. The air there smells like a very expensive soup that nobody has ever tasted.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Taste Test Lab
Beakers, spoons and a very small flag: does your deck have the body for the panel?
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The Prototype Bay smells of hot iron and burnt sugar. A war machine squats on a pallet: half oven, half cannon, one wheel still in its packing straw.
Inspection! ATTEN-TION! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations! This is not a drill, it is a souffle!
And what is THIS? A civilian. In my bay. Unsupervised. With flavour on his breath.
Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.
Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder. I have a ration meeting.
He salutes the machine. The machine salutes back with a ladle. The Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Self-Repair
When three of its units have been scrapped, the machine patches itself: it heals 2.
ASSEMBLY... INCOMPLETE... REPAIRING... YES, CHEF...
The War Machine heals 2.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The war machine sags and steams. Taped to its side is an inspection card under a seal of crossed forks: PASSED. NEEDS MORE SALT. - COL. C. CRUMB.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Corrupted Pantry
Shelves of glowing, sickly-green food hum softly. A ladle is still stirring a pot that nobody is minding, and the pot has started to hum back.
Eat the glowing stew
It is delicious. It is probably cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.
Take only the sealed jars
Some of the pantry is still clean. The jars are labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You do not open them. You sell them.
Ask the ladle to stop
It has been stirring for ten years and nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.
R&D Archives

Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way, as if written by someone who has only ever read about left-handedness.
Compare the handwriting
The chef who wrote these has never held a ladle. The impostor is exposed, and so is how little they have been cooking.
Photograph the blueprints
Evidence, and a buyer for it. The buyer asks no questions, which is the best kind of buyer.
Pocket the recipe marked DO NOT SERVE
It is one line long and ends with 'send it back.' You can see why it was classified.
The cannon-blender is fed protein and plates in equal measure. Every Ingredient and every Iron goes into the same shaker, and something six feet tall comes out.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Full Blend
On its 4th turn the cannon-blender fires a full load: you take 2 damage.
Next turn: the cannon-blender fires a full load (2 damage).
Load the smoothie! Purée setting! FIRE!
You take 2 damage.
The Grand Chef turns from the stove. She smiles the smile from every portrait in the Pantry. She has worn it for ten years without a crease.
"Ah. A taste tester. Welcome to the future of dining. The future is efficient. The future does not need to be tasted."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Do: Grand Chef of the Test Kitchen (allegedly)
Welcome to the Test Kitchen. Everything here is delicious. I have been told.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Mask Slips
At half health the disguise slips: Perfect Copy ends (its units lose +1/+1), and two 1/1 Sashimi Weenies are rushed out.
Delicious. Delicious. I have been told that is the word. ...Why will it not stay on?
Perfect Copy ends. Two 1/1 Sashimi Weenies are rushed out.
No Face of Its Own
Near the end the face it wore is gone: its units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
You never taste your own soup, do you? ...Neither do I. I cannot.
The Doppelganger falters: its units get -1/-0.
The Executive Test Kitchen
The Grand Chef's private kitchen. Her apron is spotless. Her chin is a little off.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::challeng: Four dishes are served to the panel. They want to see that you can field real, living units, not just soup.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::event.tk: The unfinished war machine fills the room: a cannon the size of a barn, fed by a conveyor belt of meatballs. A tired engineer in an apron asks whether you are here for the inspection or for the tour.
Eat one of the test meatballs
The engineer slips you the blueprints and a few coins. "Please burn these," he whispers. "After you're done selling them."
You twist the valve. The cannon coughs, sighs, and settles into a sulk. Your units feel sturdier in a kitchen that is slightly less likely to fire at them.
You eat the prototype meatball and feel much better, if slightly singed. The aftertaste has a blast radius.
A sous-chef is hiding behind the sacks of flour. "She does not taste the soup," he whispers. "She never tastes the soup.
Chef ALWAYS tastes. Whoever is in that kitchen is not our Chef."
Take his notes on the impostor
Turn him in for the reward
He presses a stained notebook into your hands: habits, weak spots, and a very detailed list of everything the impostor will not eat. The list is everything. Your units hit harder.
He eats like a man who has not eaten in a week. "Thank you," he says. "Be careful.
The real Chef is down there somewhere. I know she is." You feel better for it.
The guards pay you without a question. You pocket the coins and feel sick.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::cutscene: Welcome to the Executive Test Kitchen, taster. Ten years in this face and this apron, and not one Gourmand looked twice.
They never looked at their Chef. They looked at the food.
You never taste your own soup, do you?
...Tasting is inefficient. The orders from {capital} asked for golems, not flavour, and the Special Sauce delivers golems.
"Delicious." That is the word I was given for it. I say it often. I do not know what it means.
Then look. I have worn this face long enough.
This is what was under it. I wore her face so long that I forgot my own. There is nothing in here to taste with.
Sit down, taster. I was told to serve you.
The Doppelganger collapses, and the Special Sauce goes with it, down a drain in the floor. Somewhere in the walls, a freezer door swings open on its own.
Ten years of frost pour out, and with them a woman in chef's whites: upright, blinking and furious.
The golems straighten up. "Yes, Chef!" they say, and this time they mean the right one.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::cutscene: Ten years in a freezer, and I still remember what this soup should taste like. Let me put it right.
I do not know what to call myself. Your name was the only one I had, and now it is yours again.
I have no name or face of my own. I cannot even taste what I make.
How will they know it's you? After ten years?
Not with a speech. Not with papers. With dinner.
Stand back, all of you. Somebody get me flour, butter and the biggest oven in this building.
Before you sits a plain, golden dish, large enough to share. You smell butter and warm bread.
The first bite breaks the enchantment all through the Endless Buffet.
You watch the chefs blink at their hands. Across the Buffet, a thousand golems lower their ladles.
Come here, you. No face, no name. What you are called does not matter. What you do is what matters.
You have been my prisoner for five minutes, and you have given me no trouble. Let me give you something in return.
So take my old name. Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title.
...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly. I will try to be someone worth the name.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.doppe: You watch the chef's perfect smile slip away with her face.
Beneath it, you see a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat.
Behind the shadow, you see the unfinished war machines standing still.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::hud.obje: The Endless Buffet, free of the impostor: the Grand Pantry is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down for a hearty meal, or walk back down to town.
Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The golems are back to guarding plates, not people. The buffet is still endless.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.hub: Hub of the Endless Buffet. The Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it.
Nobody leaves hungry. Innovation Season is over. Dinner is back.
- Real food. Real sauce. Real chef.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.inn: The Grand Chef has asked us to remember that food is for eating, not for firing.
Complaints may now be submitted in sauce. We are prepared to take a little heat.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.spe: Return unused Special Sauce to the Pantry. Its ingredients have failed to establish that they are food.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.tas: The taste testers are free. They like food again. Please give them seconds.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.exi: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet - we just mopped, but your sample is yours now; take two.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.mai: Research & Development. Open to the public for tours.
The repurposed cannon now fires bread at pigeons. This is what we meant by a feeding programme.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::sign.ins: Found: a kitchen where there was a lab, a stove where there was a cannon, and a Grand Chef who was finally herself.
Passed inspection, with distinction. And dessert.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.odal: It wasn't her. It was a Doppelganger, wearing her face for ten years, and you walked right up to it. I'd have fainted. I did faint, earlier, about something else.
The real Chef is back in her own kitchen, tasting her own soup. We all cried. Say it with me: Yes, Chef. Louder. YES, CHEF! ...Oh, that felt good. We mean it this time.
She remembered the cake. The very first thing she said when we opened the freezer was "Is the boy all right?" I didn't know what to tell her.
The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef - finally an order I can stomach!
Take seconds. You've earned seconds. You've earned thirds. Listen to me, I'm not even whispering.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.tarr: Ingredients are coming back from the Test Kitchen by the cartload, even pigs! A happy pig this time; I've had enough professional disagreements.
People wave when I fetch things now! And nobody asks for cannonballs - I prefer a lighter lunch.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::npc.dolc: Madame Mirepoix, free of the sauce. My taste buds came back last week, and darling... the sugar. I wept into a meringue.
Cakes by day, cards by night. All by appointment, and all by choice.
Sit down and have a slice, darling. The cake has been promoted from decoration to dessert.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::freed_np: Have you eaten? Sit. I am the Grand Chef, and forgive the apron: the impostor kept it cleaner, but I wear it with feeling.
Ten years in the walk-in freezer, and I never once forgot the taste of honest soup. They put that sauce in every pot and called it innovation.
Innovation is a pinch of something new in something good. It is not a cannon.
Thank you for finding me. Now eat.
Let me cook for you. I promise there is nothing in it but food.
And you, my dear: you do not know your name yet. Good. That is not a flaw, it is a blank page. Go and do something worth signing.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::ruler.st: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us.
data/story/gourmand_story.tres::freed_np: Third, if you count the dishes. Chef says what I am called does not matter, only what I do. So I am doing a great many dishes.
I made a sauce today. A real one. I tasted it. As me. It had too much salt.
Everyone ate it anyway and said it was a good start. I did not know people could be so kind about salt.
I have a face of my own now. I am still deciding what to do with it. I am trying.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: The Colonel's gone. His office is empty. He took the paste recipe with him.
It's one word long. The word is 'paste'.
He left before dessert. He always did. They say he's feeding the whole Capital now, from a factory.
Grey, from a tap. Somebody ought to teach that man to cook.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.necroc: The afterlife is processing again. Agnes says the queue moved four whole numbers yesterday. We had cake.
I have a new stamp. It says HELPED. I have used it nine times. I am counting.
You may challenge me again, if you like. No permit required. That one is my favourite rule.
The barrier is down. A sign with a stamp on it says the road needs a permit. Nobody has ever been issued one.
Prudence Pallor stamps a permit, hands it over, and files the original in triplicate.
The barrier creaks up. The road to the D.N.A. is open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::necrocrat_n: Halt. This checkpoint requires a permit. Permits are not issued. Please take a number.
Your number is zero. It is always zero. Now serving: nobody.
The authorization is valid. Policy says I must stop you. I have read all of the policy. Twice.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Pruden: Your number is zero. It is always zero. Please hold.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Stamped APPROVED
At half health Prudence grabs the wrong stamp: APPROVED. You heal 3.
APPROVED. ...That was the wrong stamp. That felt... nice. Disregard.
Prudence stamps APPROVED by mistake: you heal 3.
data/story/intro_story.tres::necrocrat_n: ...I can hear my own thoughts again. I think I was Pending for a decade. Old habits die hard. Unlike me.
{villain} did not corrupt us. He used our own rules: a perfectly valid transfer of authority, notarized and filed.
The Hall of Final Approvals is at the top of the D.N.A. Go carefully. Or fill out a form. Ideally both.
Application denied; reapply in ten to twelve centuries. This is our express service.
Not yet, then. Take a number. It is still zero.

data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.courier: Urgent delivery. Signature required. Signature will be taken.
Delivering a Notice of Compliance, in triplicate. Please hold still for all three.
data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.intern:: Unpaid. Undead. Eager to impress the new management. At last, some hands-on experience.
It does not know the new management is wrong. It only knows the paperwork is valid.
data/story/dna_story.tres::enemy.manager: Has wanted a quick sync since 1994. Now enforces the new regulations with great, unenthusiastic precision.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.chest::0: You find supplies filed under Miscellaneous. For once, you meet the requirements.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_bad: The machine screams. The coffee screams. You drink it anyway. -1 HP.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_gol: A coin rolls out of the dispenser. The machine regrets nothing. +gold.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_goo: You drink the coffee. Almost drinkable. Someone may be disciplined. (+HP)
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.coffee_gre: Perfect brew! The machine seems proud of itself. Full recovery of... something.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.heal_alrea: You are already as rested as the dead get. Which is very rested. Technically, eternally.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.heal_couch: You sink into the Breakroom Couch. Somehow it is both ice cold and slightly damp. HP restored.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.main_dunge: The Executive Floor's great doors stand open a crack. Beyond them: endless desks, green lamps, and stamps that thump like heartbeats.
A voice from the dark says: PLEASE TAKE A NUMBER.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.printer_ok: The printer gives you a warm card. You accept before it can request a reference.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.printer_po: PAPER JAM. The printer regrets to inform you that your fee is non-refundable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.punch_agai: Your shift is already recorded. Please do not punch twice; the clock has suffered enough.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.punch_in::: You punch in. The clock says 'Welcome back, Pending.' A small buff glimmers on you.
