data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.suggestion: You post a suggestion. Something drops back out of the box. You appear to have been assigned the follow-up.
The suggestion box is empty now. The committee read your suggestion. It was not implemented. It was, however, laminated.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.wake::0: You wake on a Lobby couch with a 15-minute limit. A form has already been filled out in your name.
data/story/dna_story.tres::fx.wake::1: It says you are 'Pending'. It also says 'Valid'.
data/story/dna_story.tres::hud.objective: The D.N.A.: the Lobby and Breakroom are safe (pending approval). HP does not come back after battles - rest on the Breakroom Couch, or ride up to town.
Every door in the building requires a form. The authorization is valid.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.first::: first clear! here's a bonus. been in my desk since '09. finally found the right occasion to open the drawer.
it's a memory game. literally. we're all memories here. anyway.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.intro::: ok so: flip two cards at a time. find all 8 pairs in 14 moves or fewer. fewer moves, more stars. easy. ish.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.lose::0: out of moves. my virtual pet lasted an hour. want another go? you get a better deal than the pet.
data/story/dna_story.tres::match.win::0: nice flipping! top 8, number one. sorry, me. we had a good run.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.coffee::: For living staff only. Undead staff, please use the Decaf Crypt.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.cubicle_: Whoever put a coffin in 12-C: you may keep it.
Please stop billing it as 'ergonomic seating'.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.fun_day:: Reminder: Mandatory Fun Day is mandatory.
Fun that is not mandatory will not be counted as fun.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.hr::1: 'Rest in Peace' is not an approved out-of-office message.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.lunch::1: Labelled lunches are not safe. Unlabelled lunches are not safe. Lunches are not safe.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.motto::1: Our motto is "Your Death, Our Priority." Please stop saying "Your Death, Our Problem."
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.parking:: Parking Lot D has been renamed Parking Lot Dead. Please stop asking why.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.records:: To access the Records Basement, bring Form 13-B.
Form 13-B is available from Form 13-A. Form 13-A is available from nobody.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.reorg::1: Due to a restructuring, you will now report to the person who reports to you.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.reorg::2: Both of you have been dead since Tuesday. Both of you report to {villain}.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.i: Oh! A customer! Hello. Gerald, breakroom barista. Also Number 4,000,212. They're on 3. I brought a book. Several. All of them, actually.
I make coffee for people who can't taste it. Nobody ever sends a cup back. The machine in the corner is temperamental: half miracle, half a different kind of miracle.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.r: Cream? None. Sugar? None. Hope? Out of stock, but we're expecting a shipment in 2090.
Per my last email: still serving 3. I don't have email. I hope the phrase conveys that I have asked before.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.i: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. Agnes Overdue, front desk. Deceased since 1987, employee of the month since 1987. Nobody else qualified.
Take a number: yours is 4,000,213. We're serving 3. Ten years ago, {villain}'s people filed some paperwork, properly. Now the whole Department works for him.
We all know it's wrong. But the authorization is valid. Irregular things I can fight, dear. Valid things just sit there and smile at you.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.r: Back again? Loyalty is rewarded here. Not with money. With more work.
The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. It builds character.
I'd help you more, but I'd need a permit to help you, and I have it on good authority I won't get one.
Ten years ago I stamped the royal funeral forms myself. The king. The queen.
There was a third form, for the little prince. It was never filed. No remains, no certificate. Policy is very strict about that.
krrrshhh... beep-boop... sorry. dial-up greeting. forty seconds. around here, that counts as an outburst.
i'm Kyle. deceased since '09. runner-up, employee of the month, 2009. Agnes won. Agnes always wins.
fun fact: ten years ago i filed the big transfer form. didn't read it. who reads forms.
...oh. right. Necrocrats. we read forms. that's, like, our whole thing.
anyway. wanna play? flip two cards, match the pairs. i made the cards myself.
virtual pet died again. seven times this week. i'll hatch another. little egg, big commitment.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.intro: Requisitions. Clerk Ledgerbone. Junior clerk, third class, third time dying. Cards, in triplicate. All Necrocrat-issue: authorized, stamped, haunted.
The stamp is haunted. It requested a raise. The new boss denied it. The stamp is taking this personally.
No returns. No exchanges. Exceptions require Form 13-B. You've heard about 13-B.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.retur: Requisition something. Or stand near the desk. You make me look busy. Excellent work so far.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.intr: Ah. A candidate for re-certification. Director Ectomund, Compliance Examiner. I examine. It is all I do. It is all I am.
I have set the same exam for three hundred years. Four questions on the Necrocrats. Every answer is on the premises: signs, memos, the staff.
The new management asked me to remove the questions on ethics. They are not in the exam. They are also, I notice, not in the building.
Answer correctly and you will be rewarded. Answer incorrectly and you will be rewarded less. I am not a monster. I am an examiner.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.retu: Back? Statistically, you have failed already. I look forward to making it official.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.hang_i: (The poster is a skeleton on a branch. It has been there since 1650.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.safety: You are already dead. Please do not make it worse.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.synerg: Together Everyone Achieves More. Eventually. Posthumously.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.wellne: Breathe in. Breathe out. (Optional for you.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.alread: The tubes hum contentedly. Nothing left to route.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.hint::: Every junction flips after a capsule passes. The first capsule only cares about the three junctions on its own path - set those first, then work out the next.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.intro:: A wall of pneumatic tubes hums and hisses. Eight capsules wait in the intake, each stamped with its destination department.
Seven junctions sit in the lines. Every junction flips after a capsule passes through it. Set the starting position of each, then send them down.
data/story/dna_story.tres::puzzle.solved: Every soul lands in the right department. The tubes cough politely and drop a small, heavy parcel in the tray.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_aud: Director Ectomund's quiz, and one hidden stash in the filing mazes. The stashes are in the corners nobody visits. So: everywhere.
Audit closed. The auditors have gone home. They live here. They went to their desks.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Director Ectomund, Compliance Examiner
Hidden stashes lurk in the filing mazes
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Compliance Audit
Compliance is auditing and Clerk Ledgerbone can't leave the desk. Start with Director Ectomund's quiz. Bring a spare pen.
Pass Director Ectomund's Compliance quiz
Find a hidden stash in the filing mazes
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_aud: Compliance is auditing. Two things, from a fresh pair of hands. One: pass Director Ectomund's re-certification quiz. Two: find one hidden stash in the filing mazes.
I cannot leave the desk. Policy. Also, my legs are on loan to Accounts. I await their return.
The quiz, passed. A stash, found. Both boxes ticked, in ink. Oh. Oh, that's lovely.
A commendation. Do not try to cash it. Accounts enjoys that more than you would.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_bac: Three roaming staff, dear, on any floor. Processed, not promoted. Don't confuse the two. I did once, and now he's my supervisor.
The backlog is clear. It will be full again by Thursday. It's nice to have a moment, isn't it? I don't get many.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Roaming staff wander every floor
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Clear the Backlog
Agnes Overdue's backlog has gone feral and is wandering the floors. Process three roaming staff members. By duel. Per policy.
Duel roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_bac: Oh good, a presence. I have a backlog, dear, and it's a literal one: three staff went feral over a deadline from the new management. They wander the floors.
Would you process three of them? Roaming staff, any floor, by duel. We can't hurt colleagues. You aren't one. You haven't filled out the form.
Three! That clears the backlog. Do you know how many forms that closes? Neither do I. Here's your bonus, dear.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_onb: The time clock by the front desk, then the coffee machine here in the breakroom. Either order. HR isn't picky. HR is just watching.
You're one of us now. Officially. Please don't read the contract. I read it once, and I'm still in line.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The time clock by the front desk
The breakroom coffee machine
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Mandatory Onboarding
Gerald says every new hire must complete onboarding, starting at the time clock. HR will know. HR is in the walls.
Punch in at the time clock by the front desk
Pour a cup at the breakroom coffee machine
data/story/dna_story.tres::quest.dna_onb: You're new to the floor, aren't you? Then it's mandatory onboarding: punch in at the time clock by the front desk, and pour a cup from the breakroom machine.
Do not skip it. HR is in the walls, and HR reports to him now. I try not to lean on the walls. It feels like sharing too much.
Punched in, caffeinated and compliant! Onboarding complete. Here's your welcome kit.
The kit is a welcome. I said it very warmly. That was the kit.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.not_pass: Not a pass. Study the signs and come back; there is no limit on attempts. I will be here. I am always here.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.repeat::: Re-certified again. The Department pays a small processing fee for the paperwork.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.0: Zero. Impressive, in its own way. Nothing for you.
Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Neither, technically, is anyone here.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.1: One correct. Your token. My interest remains non-refundable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.2: Two. Half-credit. Half-credit is the highest honor of the Necrocrats.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.3: Three correct. One shy of perfect. Take your reward; perfect would have made me suspicious.
data/story/dna_story.tres::quiz.result.4: Four correct. Perfect. I have recorded my joy in triplicate. Please do not ask me to demonstrate it.
You are now Certified Deceased, Class A. The reward is real; the title is honorary.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.coffee::: For living staff only. Undead: use the Decaf Crypt.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.cubicle_: Please do not personalize your cubicle. Yes, haunting counts.
Hot-desking is permitted. Hot-desking has been banned. See memo.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.elevator: Floors served: Lobby, Records, Quarterly Reviews, Under Renovation.
Form 13-B required. No form, no floor.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.executiv: Staff beyond this point are dead. Executives were dead before it was fashionable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.exit::1: To {town}. Permit stamped in triplicate by Prudence Pallor. Sunlight not guaranteed. Mind the potholes.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.filing_m: If you are lost, you are in the correct place.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.fun_day:: Attendance is compulsory for all staff, including the undead.
Cake provided. Cake will not be eaten.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.lobby_ma: A Division of Afterlife Services and Labor
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.mailroom: All souls routed by pneumatic tube. Souls routed incorrectly will be re-routed. Eventually.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.main_dun: Where all things are authorized: life, death, resurrection and the afterlife.
Appointment required. Estimated wait: 400 years. Waiting room not included.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.matching: Please do not feed the Top 8.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.now_serv: (Estimated wait for number four: 400 years. The Department of Necrotic Affairs appreciates your patience.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.printer:: Out of toner. Out of body. Contact IT (deceased). Please specify which problem.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.puzzle::: Set every junction. Send the souls. Do not send them to Accounts Payable.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.quiz::1: Annual re-certification: 4 questions. Failure is not an option. It is a form.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.filed_co: A complaint, filed in 1873, about the filing system. It is filed under C, for Complaint, and also under F, for Filing, and also under P, for Pending.
The response is filed under R. The response is blank.
data/story/dna_story.tres::shrine.used::: The stamp has been used. The form is complete. Nothing else will be approved today, or any day.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.requisit: Cards, in triplicate. Souls, in quadruplicate.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.suggesti: All suggestions are read by a committee that has been dead since 1979.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.take_num: Your assigned number is a number. Requests for a better answer require a new number.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.time_clo: (Punching other employees is not covered by your plan.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.exit.body:: Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully; defeated staff will be back next time. Exit permit 12-X has been auto-approved. This time.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.exit.title: Walk back to town?
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.mini.body:: Three meetings in a row. Your HP carries from one to the next and nothing heals in between. Win all three for a unique Necrocrat card.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.mini.body_: You have already earned the unique card here. You can still sit through the meetings for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.authoriz: Form 1-A, submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain}.
This transfer is valid. If you disagree, please submit Form 1-B. Form 1-B is available from the person who wrote the transfer.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.new_mana: By order of {villain}, all personnel are required to follow all rules, permits and procedures, including the new ones.
This is not oppression. This is policy.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.permit_t: Standing in a hallway for more than 30 seconds requires a Permit to Stand (Form 7-S).
Form 7-S requires a Permit to Fill in Forms (Form 7-F). Form 7-F requires a signature. The signature requires you to stand still.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.new_rule: Rule 40,001: All rules must be followed.
Rule 40,002: All rules include this rule.
data/story/dna_story.tres::effect.buff.f: Every Necrocrat here is properly stamped, countersigned and notarized. It makes them very hard to argue with.
data/story/dna_story.tres::effect.debuff: Beefcakes do things on the spot, which here requires a permit, in triplicate, and a fee. The fee is also a form.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.title: The Hall of Final Approvals
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.body:: The Hall of Final Approvals governs life, death, resurrection and the afterlife. Its authority controls the Necrocrats. HP carries in from the zone; only the waiting room heals. Beat Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, to free the D.N.A.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.body_: The Hall of Final Approvals is open and, somehow, more efficient. You can still walk the departments for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except in the waiting room.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ui.main.butto: Take a number and go in
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Can't collect a soul in this building, dear. The paperwork won't let me past the lobby. I've been waiting since the transfer.
I took a number. Heh. It's a big one.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-LEDGERBONE.barks:: Form 12-B for purchases. Filled in correctly? Oh. Oh, that's lovely.
The stamp wants a raise. I have given it the form. It is thinking.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ECTOMUND.barks:: Three hundred years, the same quiz. The answers have never been fresher.
The ethics questions were removed by management. Ethically, I object.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-KYLE.barks::0: is it still '09 out there? no? huh. brb, updating my away message.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-KYLE.barks::1: brb, haunting. actually stay. nobody reads the 'be right back' part.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GERALD.barks::0: Four million two hundred and twelve. They're on three. Any minute now.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-GERALD.barks::1: Coffee? Nobody can taste it. I make it anyway. It's the thought.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-AGNES.barks::0: Employee of the month since 1987, dear. The plaque is getting heavy.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-AGNES.barks::1: Appeal forty thousand and one. Denied. I'm starting to take it personally.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MORTIMER.barks:: Number four million two hundred and fourteen. I have begun to understand Gerald.
I have filed my impatience in triplicate. It is still being processed.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Roaming staff wander every floor
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Gerald is Number 4,000,212 and they are on 3. Thin out the queue to the Waiting Room of Eternity: process two roaming staff.
Duel roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Number 4,000,212? That's me. They're on 3. Can you help?
The queue in the Waiting Room of Eternity is stuck. Process two of the roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors and I'll get you in. I've brought a book. Several.
Process two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move itself. I've given it a very fair chance.
Two fewer. The queue moved! Slightly. I felt it in my ticket.
The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Please leave mine; we've been through so much together.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up through cat-eye glasses, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the long deceased.
'Forms A through F,' she says. 'Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Betty: Take a number. The number is irrelevant. Take it anyway.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Forms A Through F
At half health Betty hands over forms A through F: she gains 2 Contracts and a 1/1 Zombie Temp files in.
Forms A through F. Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.
Betty gains 2 Contracts; a 1/1 Zombie Temp files in.
Out to Lunch
On her 5th turn Betty takes her lunch break: her units stand down (exhausted) for that turn, because nothing gets done on lunch.
Next turn: Betty goes on lunch (her units stand down for a turn).
I'm on lunch. Nothing happens on lunch. That includes me.
Betty is on lunch: her units are exhausted this turn.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. 'Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Don't make it a thing.'
Far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_lo: You step through the doors and a small grey machine hands you a ticket: 4,000,213. The display above the desk says NOW SERVING: 3.
A clerk looks up, sighs, and says, in a voice like a filing cabinet closing: "The authorization is valid. Please wait."
A cavernous reception. A single sign reads: ALL THINGS REQUIRE AUTHORIZATION. THIS INCLUDES THE SIGN.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_nu: A small silvery ghost is already in the queue, hugging an enormous stack of appeals tied with three kinds of ribbon. "Number 4,000,213. There you are, dear.
Gerald in the breakroom is 4,000,212. You two will be neighbours. He's a lovely man. He's been there a while.
Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. I stopped counting the appeals. Every one denied.
Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
You are number 4,000,213. They are serving number 3. It is a very long queue, and it is the only way forward.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_in: An intake clerk demands to see your paperwork. It is also a fight. It is mostly a fight.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_nu: A small silvery ghost waves from the queue, the ribboned stack of appeals under one arm. "Number 4,000,213. Saved your place, dear. Nobody noticed. Nobody ever does.
Gerald in the breakroom is 4,000,212. You two will be neighbours. He's a lovely man. He's been there a while.
I come down here on my lunch hour to appeal. Appeal number forty thousand and one. Denied. I am starting to take it personally.
Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Take-a-Number Kiosk
A small grey machine offers you a ticket. The display above says NOW SERVING 3. Your number is 4,000,213. A polite ghost behind you coughs, then apologises for coughing.
Take a number and wait
You wait. You wait some more. You feel seen, and slightly worse. A vending machine dispenses one sad cookie.
Take every number
The machine jams, apologises and coughs up coins and a written warning. You are now marked 'Difficult.'
Skip the queue
Nobody dares object. Yet. Number 4,000,213 is quietly becoming a legend.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_wa: A very comfortable waiting room. The magazines are 600 years old. Restore HP.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_au: An auditor examines your deck for compliance. Three cards will be weighed on the Scale of Approved Expenditures.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_ma: Souls arrive here by pneumatic tube when nobody knows where else to put them. They are not happy about it.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_lo: A counter piled high with misfiled belongings. A sign: IF YOU FIND SOMETHING, YOU MAY KEEP IT. IF YOU LOSE SOMETHING, SEE A CLERK.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_co: The department that enforces the rules that enforce the rules. Their officer is perfectly polite. (Elite)
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_ap: A judge in an old powdered wig weighs your case. The scales are made of paperwork.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_no: Every important document in the Hall passes through here. It must be stamped, signed and witnessed by a notary.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Waiting Room of Eternity
Row after row of chairs. Can your deck outwait the line?
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_wa: You wait until your legs ache. You check the clock above the door: four minutes.
The clock is lying. The clock was told to.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_co: The officer folds his clipboard and, with a courteous nod, points you toward the Appeals Department.
"You may appeal," he says. "You will lose. But you may appeal."
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_re: The Records Labyrinth is a canyon of filing cabinets that goes down further than it goes up. At its heart, under glass, lies the original transfer: the Necrocrat Path, signed over to {villain}.
It is flawless. Submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized, filed.
Agnes reads over your shoulder and stops at one clause. Under HEIR OF THE FORMER SOVEREIGN it says: "Deceased (presumed). Remains: not on file."
"Irregular," says Agnes, very quietly, and looks at it for a long time. "A presumed death with no remains on file is an incomplete form.
Someone should look into it, dear. This form does not tell us what happened to the boy."
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: In Triplicate
At half health the Wraith notarizes a Red Tape for itself.
Signed. Witnessed. Notarized. In triplicate. One copy is for you. You may not keep it.
The Notary Wraith gains a Red Tape.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_fo: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "Form 27-C. Third attempt. It needs a 27-B, which needs a 27-C.
They keep stamping it DENIED. Irregular, apparently. Do not mind me, dear. I have filed worse and kept the receipts."
A counter with a very long sign: FORM 13-B REQUIRES FORM 13-A. FORM 13-A REQUIRES FORM 13-B. PLEASE SEE A CLERK.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_du: Every form here has a twin. Every twin has a twin. The clerks are undead and, understandably, a bit short.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Form 27-B Office
Form 27-B requires Form 27-C, which requires a stamp from the office you are standing in. A clerk slides a pen across the counter without looking up.
Fill out the forms
Everything is in order. A boon is granted and a small tax is levied, in that order, by two different departments.
Forge the stamp
It works! Mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves, loudly, with a stapler.
Ask the clerk what Form 27-C is
The clerk looks up for the first time in decades. Nobody has ever asked. She slides you a Pink Slip 'for personal use' and, you swear, winks.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_cl: Undersecretary Vellum squares his papers and does not look up. "Noted. You wish to challenge the transfer of authority.
The authorization remains valid. It was submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. You may appeal in triplicate."
"Mr. Grimsby has asked me to hold the Court until his schedule opens. I will hold it very, very well. Noted."
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Noted.
At half health Vellum files an objection: he gains a Contract.
Noted. ...Noted?
Vellum gains a Contract.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_cl: The Appeals Court's Undersecretary Vellum, Mortimer's deputy, defends the transfer of authority to the last paragraph. He has never once been thanked. (Elite)
Vellum squares his papers with great care. "Noted," he says, very quietly. "The authorization remains valid."
For the first time, it sounds like a question.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Shredding Room
Rows of paper shredders chew through the day's denied appeals. A sign reads: SHRED ONE THING, RECEIVE ONE THING. Another, in smaller letters, reads: THINGS INCLUDE YOU.
Shred a spare appeal
The shredder hums happily and pays out in coins. It says 'denied' in a voice like a kettle.
Shred your own number
Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter, and slightly nonexistent. The machine files you under 'Resolved.'
Reach in for what it ate
You pull out half of a lost appeal. It is, technically, a weapon. The machine takes a bite of you in exchange.
The elevator is hand-cranked by a Beefcake on loan from the wheels. Every floor needs a permit and a rep. Iron turns the crank; Red Tape keeps the doors shut.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, looks up from an infinite pile of paperwork. His face is as smooth as a blank form. His stamp is the size of a tombstone.
"You do not have an appointment. That is irregular. However, the authorization is valid, and under it every visitor is entitled to a hearing.
The answer is no. The question is irrelevant. Please state your case anyway.
You have, according to the clock, four hundred years."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Mortim: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant. Please state your case anyway.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Mortimer Files a Form
On his 4th turn Mortimer files Form 27-B: a 1/1 Filing Clerk is hired to process it.
Next turn: Mortimer files Form 27-B (a clerk is hired).
Your appeal has been received, reviewed and denied. It was a very good appeal.
A 1/1 Filing Clerk is hired.
Filed on a Tuesday
Late in the fight Mortimer finds a note under his own form: FILED ON A TUESDAY. His units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The authorization is valid. It was filed on a Tuesday. ...We do not file on Tuesdays.
Mortimer hesitates over the form: his units get -1/-0.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: A vast office with a single desk, a single stamp, and one very patient authority.
data/story/dna_story.tres::challenge.ha_: The auditor lays three cards on the Scale of Approved Expenditures. A reasonable total will be stamped. An unreasonable one will be fined.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_take: You hold ticket 4,000,213. The display says NOW SERVING: 3. The queue snakes through the lobby, up the stairs and out of a window.
A clerk offers you a form, a coffee and a pitying look.
Wait your turn (it will be a while)
You wait. And wait. A clerk takes pity, and the polite ghost ahead of you shares a biscuit and apologises that it is stale.
You are called in, eventually, rested and a little richer. Waiting, in the Hall, is a kind of work.
The Expedite Fee is an official fee, with an official receipt. A tiny clerk stamps your ticket and a door opens. You feel oddly refreshed.
You cut in line. Forty thousand undead clerks turn and glare. You are processed immediately, and a little roughly.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_form: Form 13-B
To pass the counter you need Form 13-B. The clerk says Form 13-B requires a Form 13-A, which she will gladly give you, once you have submitted Form 13-B.
Ask for Form 13-A
Pay the clerk 25 gold to look the other way
"Form 13-A," she says. "Certainly. It requires a Form 12-F, which requires a strong cup of tea."
She does not look the other way. She looks at the gold. The gold is accepted.
She stamps something you cannot read, and the way ahead opens.
Form 12-F
Form 12-F is available at the Counter of Form 12-F. The Counter of Form 12-F is closed until Form 13-B has been filed.
Ask for Form 11-D
Argue
"Form 11-D," she says. "A simple form. It requires only your signature, in blood.
Please do not worry. Blood is optional. The signature is not."
You argue. A tiny stamp appears from nowhere and hits you. It hurts a little.
The clerk says: "That was a warning. The authorization is valid."
Form 11-D
Form 11-D is the last form in the chain. It is one line long: "I, the undersigned, request Form 13-B." You sign.
A stamp thunders. Forms 13-B, 13-A and 12-F all appear at once, in perfect order.
Submit all the forms and claim the reward
Rest in the clerk's break room instead
Every form passes. A bureaucrat's tear of joy lands on the ink. You receive a stamped Form 13-B, a small refund and a commendation you cannot read.
The clerk's break room is the most efficient room in the Hall. You are given a cup of tea, a biscuit and a lovely, quiet chair. You feel ready for the next department.
data/story/dna_story.tres::event.ha_nota: A very old notary sits behind a very high counter, a seal in one hand and a very large quill in the other. "Everything in the Hall," he says, "must be notarized.
Lie down in the notary's cot
Sell the notary a spare seal
The seal comes down with a THUMP. You are, officially, a person. Your units feel more legitimate, and hit a little harder for it.
The cot is small, hard and incredibly comfortable. You sleep for a very official ten minutes, and wake refreshed, with the notary's seal printed on one cheek.
He pays in cash, takes no receipt, and tells you he never saw you. You have never felt more notarized.
data/story/dna_story.tres::dungeon.ha_bo: The stamp falls from Mortimer's hand, and the paperwork goes still.
At the very bottom of the pile, under every form, every stamp and every signature, is a small note in a trembling hand: FILED ON A TUESDAY.
"...Oh," says Mortimer. "Oh, no. Tuesday is not a business day in this building.
The authorization was valid. It was always valid. But the office is vacant, and policy is policy."
data/story/dna_story.tres::cutscene.vaca: The CE-No has been removed from office. By policy, the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment. I will look it up.
...It is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.
Me? Oh, for pity's sake. I filed more appeals than anyone alive or dead, and this is how they reward it?
I only ever wanted to leave.
The procedure is clear. The office passes to you, and I am afraid you cannot appeal it. I would have to deny it.
...Then I will stay, Mortimer. Not for you. I will stay until nobody waits as long as I did.
Even the dead deserve humanity. Our job is to help the lost souls. We have an obligation to help.
Following orders be damned. We treat everyone with respect.
Then we write a new one. Take a number, Mortimer. You are right behind Gerald.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.appro: You hear the great DENIED stamp crack. For the first time in the Department's long afterlife, it does not come down.
Forms rise around you. Across the Department, a thousand clerks look up from their desks.
Somewhere nearby, you hear a pen stop scratching.
the queue moved. like, actually moved. my number's coming up in only four hundred years. new personal best.
anyway. wanna play? one more round before i pass on. jk. unless?
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.quiz.retu: Back again. The Department has reopened its records to honest examination, so I examine with a clear conscience now.
Statistically, you will still fail a question. Statistically, I will still enjoy it. Some things are not corruption. They are personality.
data/story/dna_story.tres::hud.objective: The D.N.A., liberated on a technicality: the Lobby and Breakroom are safe. HP does not come back after battles - rest on the Breakroom Couch, or ride up to town.
Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully. You no longer need an exit permit. Nobody does. We are still a little scared of the pen.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.lobby_ma: A Division of Afterlife Services and Labor
Authority Restored (Authorization Revoked on a Technicality)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.authoriz: Form 1-A has been found to be filed on a Tuesday. Tuesday is not a business day in this building.
The transfer is void. Thank you for your patience. Please ignore the previous notice, the notice before that, and the notice about the notices.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.new_mana: Back from retirement, and delighted to be here. Rules and procedures have been reduced from 40,000 to a more reasonable 39,000.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.permit_t: Standing, sitting and lying down are now permitted. Please choose for yourself. We realise this may take practice.
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.now_serv: (The number machine has been switched off. Please just come in.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::sign.main_dun: Formerly where all things were authorized. The doors are now open, and the form is optional.
Estimated wait: some minutes. Waiting room included, with magazines.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.i: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. Old habits, dear. Ghosts were never good at being in one place.
Mortimer is in the Waiting Room, number 4,000,214. He is learning to wait. It is going about as well as you would expect.
That unfiled form. I kept it in my drawer for ten years, just in case. I think I'll keep it there a little longer. Something tells me it won't be needed.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.dolores.r: The authorization is still valid. But there is a rule above it now: help people.
Prudence is my deputy. She is much nicer than she used to be, and so, I hear, am I.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.i: Oh! It's you! Gerald, barista, and as of this morning, Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I didn't know what to do with my hands. So I made coffee.
Agnes switched the queue machines off and called every number herself, one by one. It took all night. She never sat down.
Have a cup. It's free. The machine is feeling generous, and so am I.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.barnaby.r: Cream? None. Sugar? None. Hope? Back in stock. I am trying not to use it all at once.
My number's been called. I'm only here because I like the coffee.
Mortimer is Number 4,000,214 now. You were 213, in between us. Don't mention it to him. He goes very quiet.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.intro: Requisitions. Clerk Ledgerbone. The stamp has stopped haunting. It got its raise.
It doesn't know what to do with itself. Neither do I. Cards, in triplicate, as always.
data/story/dna_story.tres::npc.pip.retur: Apparently I am allowed to be unbusy now. I keep reaching for the stamp to certify it.
Practising. Just stood here for a minute. Nothing was filed. Exhilarating.
data/story/dna_story.tres::memo.new_rule: Rules 40,001 through 40,003 have been repealed. Please allow a moment for the notices to catch up.
data/story/dna_story.tres::poster.compli: (Freedom is also fine. Choose what you like.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.agn: Agnes Overdue, head of the D.N.A. Yes, me. The office goes to the senior-most applicant, and I filed more appeals than anyone. I have never been so annoyed to win.
I only wanted to leave. I will. Soon. But first I'm fixing this place, so nobody else waits as long as I did.
Even the dead deserve humanity. Our job is to help the lost souls. Following orders be damned: we treat everyone with respect.
And you, dear. You were a number in somebody's file once, weren't you? I can see it in how you hold your shoulders.
Never let anyone file you under 'subject' again.
data/story/dna_story.tres::ruler.statue:: Statue pending approval. Do not look at it until it has been approved.
(Authorization revoked. The statue has been asked to leave. It has taken a number.)
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.pru: Prudence Pallor, Deputy Head of the Department. Yes, I stamped DENIED on everything. I was tired, the paperwork was valid, and I am sorry.
{villain} did not corrupt us, you know. He used our own rules. Now I stamp APPROVED on things that deserve it.
The stamp is lighter than I remembered. Do you have anything I can approve?
data/story/dna_story.tres::freed_npc.mor: Mortimer Grimsby. Formerly CE-No. Currently number 4,000,214 in the Waiting Room of Eternity. Gerald was 4,000,212.
You had 4,000,213. You did not wait. I keep thinking about that.
I made others wait far longer. It is worse knowing that now.
The authorization was valid. I have begun to wonder whether that was ever the right question.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Intake's moving again! Agnes waved me straight through. First time in ten years nobody asked me for Form 27-B. Heh.
data/story/intro_story.tres::gate.refuse: Archdruid Compostella is herself again. She hugged me. She smells like rain and a little bit like compost. Perfect.
Most of the thorns are gone; I keep one in a pot. It's behaving, but I'm not ready to let it meet the curtains.
Want a practice round? I promise not to thorn at you. Much. The raccoons are judging, so be nice.
A wall of thorns has swallowed the forest path. It looks like it is breathing.
Moss Mulligan lays a hand on the thorns. They sigh, brown, and crumble into leaf mould.
The forest path to the Verdant Dump is open.
data/story/intro_story.tres::refusemance: ...the green is hungry... the green is HUNGRY... nothing goes to waste...
The Rot keeps this path for the Rotheart. Turn back. Turn back. Turn... into compost.
If you will not leave, the hungry green will keep you. Forever. Very nicely. Like mulch.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Moss M: ...the green is hungry... stay... stay and be fed...
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Did I Thorn at You?
At half health the real Moss breaks through for a moment: the thorns loosen and you heal 3.
...grow... GROW... (small) Did I thorn at you? I'm sorry, I can't make it stop...
The thorns loosen: you heal 3.
data/story/intro_story.tres::refusemance: Oh. Oh no. Did I thorn at you? I'm so sorry. The Rot speaks very softly, right up until it doesn't.
The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything else grew out from her.
The path is clear. Go gently in there. And if you see a raccoon, say hi. They're very good boys.
...the green is patient... it has all the time in the world... and so does the garbage...
...come back... the green can wait... it has nowhere to leaf...
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::ZONE_M: Root Cause
A wall of thorns has swallowed the forest path, and the druid guarding it sounds very wrong. Clear the way and find what is making the Dump sick.
Uproot Moss Mulligan at the thorn wall
The thorn wall across the forest path
Walk the forest path into the Verdant Dump
The withered thorn wall on the forest path
Lend a hand: finish a favour in the Verdant Dump
Billie Muckfoot, Granny Gristle or Brother Bramble
Descend into the Rotheart
The way down into the Rotheart, at the bottom of the Dump
The Verdant Dump: the Compost Grange is safe, though the vines keep trying the door. HP does not come back after battles - sit down to a fresh harvest meal, or walk back down to town. The Rotheart festers somewhere to the north.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.m: Three levels down, one after another. Your HP carries from one level to the next and nothing heals in between. Reach the bottom for a unique Refusemancer card.
You already took the unique card from the landfill. You can still dig for gold and XP. HP carries over; nothing heals in between.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.e: Leaving the Verdant Dump ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, scarecrows and gulls (all a little too alive) will be back next time, and so will the garbage.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.m: The path to the Rotheart is a tunnel of living roots. The air is warm, wet and humming.
Something very large is breathing, somewhere underneath. It is not you.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. You are thoroughly farm-fed. HP restored.
You are already full of HP. Granny Gristle offers you a third helping anyway. It is a very small turnip.
SCREEEE! A mutant junk gull dive-bombs you and steals your dignity. (-2 HP)
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.w: You wake face-down in a haybale at the Compost Grange. Granny Gristle is leaning on a pitchfork, chewing a stalk of something.
"Fell over in the muck, dearie. We rolled you out. Mucking-out fee is yours. Call it a soil charge. Heh!
Haybale was free. Mind you, it is growing. Best get up before you put down roots."
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You find a treasure chest among the rubbish. For once, sorting pays.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.p: You already took the one lying here. Come back next visit; the Dump restocks itself overnight. It is very good at that.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: The bin burps, steams and hands you a warm Compost Cocktail. It smells like a promise. You feel sturdier. (+1 max HP this visit)
The Compost Bin needs two piles of good junk. You have fewer than two. It waits for you to get your scrap together.
The bin is full of cocktails for this visit. Come back next visit. It will have fermented.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.s: You kneel. A seed in the shrine splits and blooms. A druid voice that sounds like moss says: "Grow."
You feel taller. (+1 max HP this visit, and a little healing)
The shrine has blessed you this visit. Give the seed a chance to enjoy being a flower.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.t: The animals fall on the junk, chew it thoughtfully, and spit out a coin. Gold!
The trough is empty. The animals are staring at you. Bring a pile of good junk.
The animals are full. One goat is lying on its back. Come back next visit.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You need a sack of fertilizer to plant a crop. The soil has standards. Low, fragrant standards.
You plant a crop and pat the soil. It wriggles a little. Come back in a bit and it will be ready.
The crop is still growing. A sprout waves at you. You give it space; it seems rather attached to the plot.
A ripe harvest! Pumpkins, melons, one suspicious turnip.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: The goat looks at you, looks at the pen, looks at the sign it was eating, and trots home. Round one: you.
The pig is exactly where you expected, in the only puddle. A little shoving and it waddles home, offended.
The raccoon walks to the pen on its hind legs, tin can held like a briefcase. You appear to be its next appointment.
That one is already back in the pen. It is sulking. It will get over it.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.b: The vine bridge sways and creaks cheerfully. It is made of vines, ambition and a lot of compost.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.g: The seed cracks. The soil heaves. Green shoots race into the air, twisting and knotting...
It has grown! You try to picture the spot without it. The druids look pleased with themselves.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.c: You climb the beanstalk, hand over hand. The leaves are big enough to sit on. Do not sit on them.
You slide down the beanstalk. Leaf, leaf, leaf, ground. It is faster than the chute and much less dignified.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.m: You swing up onto the saddle. Faster, and it can smash junk barricades. Press Q to dismount.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.d: You hop off and the animal trots back to its stable, snorting.
You cannot dismount out here, the scree will eat your boots. Find a flat spot first.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.b: A barricade of junk. Far too heavy to push on foot. Something fast and stubborn could charge through it.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.s: KA-RASH! Tyres fly, doors fly, and a very surprised hubcap lands in the pen. The way is open.
KA-SPLOOSH! The dam bursts and the recycling stream flows free, along with half a mattress.
You land in a pile of leaves. You decide not to examine the softer bits.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::fx.h: You fall in! Someone fishes you out with a pitchfork. You drip on dry ground. (-1 HP)
Fell into %s - fished out at the last safe spot, 1 damage to zone HP.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::bark: Mind the edge. The river's lovely to look at and a nightmare to climb out of.
Compost doesn't sort itself. Well. Lately it tries. That's the problem.
If a raccoon in a crown asks for your lunch, say no. He'll cry. Still no.
New stairs. Same climb. I was hoping they would fix that.
Every terrace a little higher, every terrace a little weirder. That's the Dump for you.
The beans came up purple again. I've stopped asking the beans.
Those purple trees were green last spring. Nobody's talking about it.
Stall's open! Patched awnings, patched prices. The holes are free.
Mind the vine ladders in the wind. They hold. Mostly.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::grow: Druid Sorrel clasps her hands. "You brought Billie's herd home? The goat, the pig and that raccoon? Then the stream owes you a bridge."
She plants her staff in the bank, whispers to it, and the vines begin to climb.
Druid Sorrel shakes her head gently. "I only grow bridges for people who have helped the herd, and Billie Muckfoot's animals have got out again.
Round them up for Billie, then come back to me, and I will grow you a way across."
A sprout mound, freshly turned. You press a Magic Bean into the soil and step back.
A sprout mound with a sign: PLANT A MAGIC BEAN HERE. You do not have one. Beans lie around the Dump, one per visit per field.
Another sprout mound. You press a Magic Bean into the soil and step back.
A sprout mound with a sign: PLANT A MAGIC BEAN HERE. You do not have a bean.
A sprout mound at the foot of Mount Scrapmore. You plant a Magic Bean. Something deep in the junk begins to rumble.
A sprout mound at the foot of the junk mountain. It wants a Magic Bean, and you are fresh out.
A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. You plant a Magic Bean and wait. Above, a hubcap spins.
A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. It wants a Magic Bean. Beans are the currency of the Dump.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: THE COMPOST GRANGE
Hub of the Verdant Dump. The Refusemancers handle waste removal and agriculture.
Nothing goes to waste. Everything, lately, goes to the Rot. Please keep the doors shut.
TODAY'S COMPOST
- Waste removal (by goat)
- Agriculture (by magic)
- Nothing goes to waste. Not even the menu.
- Do not water anything. It is already awake.
THE FOREST PATH
To {town}, past Moss Mulligan's thorn wall. Sort your boots. Check for vines; they will claim to be laces.
THE HARVEST MEAL
Sit. Eat. Do not ask where the carrots were last Tuesday.
GRANNY GRISTLE'S SWAP SHED
One person's trash is another person's starting hand. Please shuffle outdoors.
THE COMPOST BIN
Two piles of good junk make one Compost Cocktail.
Do not drink the compost. Do drink the Cocktail.
THE DRUID SHRINE
Kneel. Be blessed. Do not step on the seedlings. They are listening.
FEEDING TROUGH
Please do not feed the goats (they will eat the sign).
A pile of good junk, however, is welcome.
BORIS THE GIANT BOAR
Fast, loyal and entirely unbothered by fences. They bother him once, briefly.
Ride him. Dismount with Q.
THE REFUSEMANCER'S OATH
We are the Refusemancers, druids of the kingdom.
We summon animals to eat its garbage and turn it into fertilizer.
We use our magic to help the crops grow. Nothing goes to waste.
THE PATCHWORK FIELDS
Every patch grows something different. Every patch is fertilized by the same goat.
PLANT A CROP
A sack of fertilizer plus time makes a harvest. Visit-length time. Do not stare at it.
THE APPLIANCE GROVE
A druid circle of old fridges and washing machines. The spirits of dishwashers are strong here.
Druid Thistlewick keeps the Dump's questions.
THE COUNTY FAIR GROUNDS
Blue ribbons for the best pumpkin, the best pie and the best pile.
Judge: Recycle Rhonda. Do not argue with the judge.
SORT IT OUT! - TODAY ONLY
Compost, metal, glass or paper. Twenty pieces, one conveyor.
The belt has never lost a piece of sleep over your performance.
MOUNT SCRAPMORE
A junk mountain, overgrown with moss and ambition.
Plant a bean at the mound to climb. Slide down the chute to leave.
BEANSTALK RULES
1. Plant bean.
2. Wait.
3. Climb. Do not look down, do not look up, do not look at the cow.
THE RECYCLING STREAM
Everything the kingdom threw away ends up here, rinsed.
Crossing: vine bridges only.
WARNING: STREAM
Do not swim, wade or ask what is in it.
If you fall in, somebody will fish you out. It costs 1 HP.
WEST BRIDGE
Not grown yet? Plant a Magic Bean at the mound beside it.
CENTRE BRIDGE
Druid Sorrel grows this one for anyone who helps Billie Muckfoot round up the herd.
EAST BRIDGE
Not grown yet? Plant a Magic Bean at the mound beside it.
THE NORTH BANK
Welcome to the far side. The wall of tyres ahead has three gaps. One has been plugged with junk.
THE JUNK DAM
Somebody has dumped half a landfill across the feeder channel.
Needs a charging mount. Brother Bramble will pay.
GIDEON THE GIANT GOAT
Eats anything. Climbs anything. Rams anything.
Do not feed him the sign.
JUNK BARRICADE
A pile of tyres, doors and ambition across the gap.
The Landfill Depths are beyond. Bring something that charges.
RUST PEAK YARDS
The finest rust in the kingdom. Small batch. Very slow finish.
THE LANDFILL DEPTHS
Three levels. Mandatory. Bring a nose peg.
Do not dig deeper than the raccoons. They will consider it competitive.
THE ROTHEART
The source of the sickness. Do not enter. Do not breathe deeply. Do not lick anything.
The deeper you go, the more it grows.
NOTE FROM A DRUID
The door is warm because something in there is thriving. It is thriving very, very hard. It is thriving at us. Please do not open it.
THE SEED SHRINE
Plant a seed in a plot and it flips that plot and its four neighbours.
Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.
THE SCREE FIELDS
Loose rubble, jagged tin and thistles. Impassable on foot.
Mounts only. Boots are not covered.
SCREE RULES
No walking. No dismounting. No dropping your lunch.
The scree will find it.
TODAY'S JUNK
Tyres, fridges, one (1) piano.
Nothing goes to waste. Everything goes to the Dump.
NOTE
Good stuff in the hollow log. If you can read this, kindly take one step back from my retirement.
- a raccoon
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::enem: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. This is no place for a cool head.
A scarecrow druid faces you, a cabbage growing where its heart should be. You see no crows. The garden has bigger problems.
Four junk gulls guard a stolen can, shrieking over its crop of mushrooms. You have interrupted a very small turf war.
Welcome to the Compost Grange. Brother Bramble, Warden of the Stream. Please close the door behind you. And lock it. And check the window.
We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals eat the kingdom's garbage and turn it into fertilizer, and our magic helps the crops grow.
Our magic runs through nature itself, and {villain} used it against us. Our Archdruid, Compostella, went first. Something got into her roots.
Now nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil. Everything is too alive, and the whole Dump is sick with growing. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
Back at the Grange? Sort your boots: compost, metal, glass, paper. Check for tendrils. We already have enough houseplants.
The Archdruid planted a tree for every royal birthday. There is a row of them past the stream. Eleven trees. Then nothing.
I water the twelfth spot anyway. I couldn't tell you why. It feels as if somebody is still coming.
Not long ago, somebody carried a sleeping young man through these woods at night. He glowed, faintly. Four colours.
The raccoons saw. Raccoons see everything.
Granny Gristle, junk-trader! Born in a haybale, raised in a barn, retired to a shed. This is the shed. It's started growing. It's got a window I never put in.
Everything here's Refusemancer-issue: grown, composted, well rinsed. Found, not stolen, dearie. The raccoon found it. I just held it very tightly.
Cards grown strong, rinsed well, faint smell of earth. Hear that hum? Well, I never promised a silent auction. Heh!
Shop's open, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
They're looking at me again. I prefer a root vegetable that minds its own business. Heh!
Oh good, a pair of legs! Billie Muckfoot, animal handler. Like the goat. I speak fluent goat. It's mostly screaming. Lately it's about the plants: the fields keep trying to eat my herd.
The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely. Ask rudely. They don't speak either. Good, sensible animals.
Any luck with the herd? Look for the goat first. It'll be eating something it shouldn't. If the thing is eating it back, shout.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Escaped animals graze out in the fields
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Round Up the Herd
Three of Billie Muckfoot's animals got out: a goat, a pig and a raccoon with a briefcase. Shoo each one back to the pen before the Rot gets them.
Shoo escaped animals back to the pen
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Three of my animals got out: a goat, a pig and a raccoon with a briefcase. The Rot's in the fields and they're wandering right into it.
Find each one out in the Dump and walk it back towards the pen before dark. Don't chase. Walk firmly. Make eye contact.
Animals respect eye contact. Raccoons consider it the start of negotiations.
Three escapees, out in the fields. The goat is eating something. The pig is in a puddle. The raccoon is writing a strongly worded letter.
All three home! The pen's never looked so full. Here's your reward.
A goat card. You can play this one without having to catch it afterwards.
The herd's home and it's plotting. Thanks! Druid Sorrel at the centre bridge will grow you a crossing now. Tell her I sent you.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Try the fields, the east edge and across the stream
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Fertilizer Run
Granny Gristle is out of fertilizer and the crops are sulking. Gather three sacks from around the Dump. Hold your nose. Hold the sack.
Gather fertilizer sacks around the Dump
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Now then, fertilizer. The crops are sulking and the soil's gone strange, and good clean fertilizer is the one thing the Rot can't grow in.
I need three sacks from around the Dump. They're lying where the animals left them. Don't ask how. I never have. Heh!
Three sacks of fertilizer, dearie. Try the fields, the east edge and the far side of the stream. Follow your nose. Then apologise to it.
Three whole sacks! The crops are going to sing. Not literally.
Mostly not. Here's your reward. Found, not stolen. Heh!
The fields are fed. Plant your own with a sack of fertilizer and a little patience. Can't sell you patience. Nobody stays to browse it.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The stables: borrow a mount, then charge the dam
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Unblock the Stream
Somebody dumped a junk dam across the feeder channel on the north bank. Borrow a mount from the stables and charge it. Brother Bramble's compost boots are the prize.
Ride a mount into the junk dam on the north bank
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ques: Somebody dumped a dam of junk across the feeder channel on the north bank, and the stream cannot breathe. Borrow a mount from the stables, charge the dam, and my compost boots are yours.
The junk dam on the north bank. Ride the goat from the north stable and charge it. Do not slow down. Dams can smell hesitation.
The stream is flowing! It is practically dancing. Here: compost boots, still warm. They squelch with pride.
The stream is clear. For now. The kingdom will refill it by Thursday. That is why we are here.
Ah, a visitor. Druid Thistlewick, Keeper of the Dump's Questions. I have sat in this ring of old appliances for forty years.
The dishwasher and I have an understanding. Lately it talks back. Forty years, and NOW it wants to clear the air.
Four questions about the Refusemancers, their work and their oath. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Verdant Dump.
Sort your thoughts like your bins: compost, recycle, regret. Answer well for gold and seeds. Answer poorly for a gentle, rustling sigh.
Back to improve your score? Good. A druid is just a student who never left the garden.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::quiz: Zero. We have found room for growth. Rather a lot of room. No reward this time.
The signs are patient. I am slightly less so. The dishwasher is not patient at all.
One. A single seed. Plant it, water it, and try again.
Two. Half-grown. Keep tending those thoughts; we are not harvesting excuses.
Three! Nearly in bloom. Take your reward and a sprig of mint.
FOUR! A perfect harvest! You may now call yourself a Certified Refusemancer, First Class.
Your reward is real. The certificate is compostable. When you tire of showing it off, let it become something humble.
Another round! The Dump pays a small fee for repeat scholarship.
Not a pass. Walk the Verdant Dump, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.
Step RIGHT up to the County Fair's own SORT IT OUT! I'm Recycle Rhonda: fair judge, pie inspector, and the finest dumpster-diver in three counties!
I voiced Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad back in the nineties! Nobody knew! All that fame went to a badger in a cape!
The Rot cancelled the pumpkin contest. It can't cancel ME! Today's show: twenty pieces of junk, one conveyor, four bins. Compost, metal, glass or paper!
Send each piece to the right bin before it falls off the end. Rewards by performance, plus a first-time bonus. Gloves on!
Back for another run, champ? The conveyor is hungry. The bins are patient. I have pie.
Remember: one person's trash is another person's blue ribbon. Sort fast. Sort true. Sort with a smile!
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sort: Twenty pieces of junk ride the conveyor. Send the front piece to the right bin (click a bin, or keys 1-4 or the arrow keys) before it reaches the end. A wrong bin or a miss breaks your streak. A long streak scores more.
Feel the rhythm of the belt!
Compost left, metal down, glass up, paper right!
No hesitation! Give that rubbish somewhere to be!
BLUE RIBBON sorting! Reduce! Reuse! Refuse to quit! All three goats in the crowd are cheering. Or hungry.
Your very first run at the fair! Here's your bonus, free, no obligation. It's a salve.
Compost salve! Rub it in! The salve, champ. Not the victory.
Not quite a run, champ. That's fine. The belt isn't going anywhere.
Unlike the jam jar. The jam jar went everywhere.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::grow: Twenty-five plots of garden sit in a five-by-five square, some bare and some in bloom. Plant a seed in a plot and that plot and its four neighbours flip between bare and bloom. Bring every plot into bloom to wake the great beanstalk.
Work from the top row down: if the plot above a bare plot is bare, plant right below it. Then fix the last row with the first row. Count your seeds; there are only four solutions.
Every plot blooms at once. The beanstalk rises, shakes out a seed pouch the size of a satchel, and hands it down with a leaf. It is still warm.
The garden is in full bloom. Nothing left to plant.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: WARNING: THE ROT
Plants here are unnaturally alive. Fungi mutate. Roots invade structures, hands, and lunch.
Do not feed anything. Do not name anything. Do not turn your back on the zucchini.
THE CORRUPTION SPREADS FROM THE NORTH
Whatever our Archdruid has become, it is feeding the whole Dump.
Follow the dying fields. Then follow the living ones. They are worse.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::effe: The Dump is alive in all the wrong ways, but its own druids know how to make the best of it.
Everything delicate rots fast in the Dump. Gourmand food does not keep. Gourmand golems keep even less.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.m: At the Rotheart, the Archdruid is joined to the Dump through its corrupted roots. HP carries in from the zone; only clean soil heals you. Beat the Archdruid to free the Verdant Dump.
The Rotheart is silent, and the roots are only roots. You can still wander the tunnels for gold and XP. HP carries in from the zone; nothing heals except on the clean soil.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Nothing has died in this valley in ten years. Not a beetle. Not a leaf. Unnatural, that.
I've taken up knitting. Heh.
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-GRISTLE.barks::0: Found, not stolen, dearie! The raccoon found it. I just held on tight. Heh!
data/npcs/npcs.json::V-GRISTLE.barks::1: Shed grew another room, dearie. At last, a growing business I don't have to water. Heh!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-THISTLEWICK.bar: Every thought has a bin. Most of mine go in compost. That is not a complaint.
The dishwasher talks back. I listen. Wisdom sometimes arrives with a rinse cycle.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RHONDA.barks::0: Reduce! Reuse! Recy-CLUE: that one goes in the green bin!
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-RHONDA.barks::1: Captain Compost Badger says: rinse first! ...Who says I do the voice?
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-BRAMBLE.barks::: The vines whisper now. It's not right. Also SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
Eleven little trees in a row, one per birthday. Then nobody came for the twelfth.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-COMPOSTELLA.bar: Everything grows back, child. Even me. Especially me.
About the barn... I will help mend it. The goat may prefer that I begin elsewhere.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Scavengers prowl the junk heaps
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Little paw prints, a tiny crown, and no compost. Drive off two scavengers to follow the trail.
Drive off scavengers in the Dump
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. Little paw prints. A tiny crown.
Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and the trail will lead you to the alley under the big dumpster. Gently, please. They're only hungry. And GUILTY.
Two scavengers in the Dump. Fresh paw prints, freshly stolen compost. A trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it. I KNEW it.
Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from a bicycle wheel. That's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Bring a peg for your nose.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Courtier collects the crusts the kingdom leaves behind and serves them back, warmed, as a royal tasting menu.
The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.
'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::His Ma: Sovereign of the Throne of Lids
Kneel before the Throne of Lids. Or crouch. Crouching is also acceptable.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Royal Bins
At half health the royal guard of bins rallies: a 1/1 Rat joins and he gains a Garbage.
WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... audited it. Orally. GUARDS!
A 1/1 Rat joins; His Majesty gains a Garbage.
Sweating Profusely
Near the end His Majesty starts to sweat: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The compost was for the kingdom. We are the kingdom. Checkmate. ...Is it warm in here?
His Majesty's units get -1/-0.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: His Majesty abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne.
'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The vines part for you, slowly. They do not seem to be letting you in. They seem to be letting you go deeper.
Behind you, the gate closes with a soft, wet sound. Somewhere ahead, something very large breathes in, and the whole tunnel breathes with it.
The Withered Gate
The entrance is a cracked archway wrapped in black-green vines. They tighten as you pass.
The Overgrown Outskirts
Normal-looking plants, mostly. They are a little too green. Everything is alive in a way that feels like it is watching you.
The Mutant Grove
Mushrooms the size of sheds. Some of them are looking at you. Some of them have hats.
The Whispering Mushrooms
A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. They know your name. They are not sure why.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Strangled Greenhouse
The vines are choosing who gets through. Can your deck keep its footing?
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: The mill wheel is gripped by roots as thick as a cart. Someone has been trimming them. Very neatly. Into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.
Mind the topiary, dear. That's His Perfection from the left. The right side is still growing in.
Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I outlawed composting. So untidy. All that rot, lying about in heaps, being honest.
Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed, a gift. Life that never ends. She was so very sad, and now nothing ever has to go.
And now, dear, I'm afraid I have a weed to remove.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Horten: Such a pretty weed. Such a shame. Do hold still, dear.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Regulation Topiary
At half health Clipwell trims two topiaries into guards: two 1/1 Topiaries join her (Prize Topiary makes them 2/2).
Such a pretty weed. Such a shame. Now, stand still while I tidy you.
Two Topiaries join Clipwell.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges. I shall send a note.
She opens a wide green umbrella, steps neatly over the roots and walks away up the ravine toward the Capital road, not one hair out of place.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: Nothing here has rotted in ten years. The pool is full of leaves that stay green, fruit that never softens, and a smell like a held breath.
Brother Bramble's notes are pinned to a root: 'NOTHING ROTS. NOTHING FEEDS THE SOIL. THE SOIL IS STARVING.
IT IS ALIVE. IT IS ALL TOO ALIVE. AND WHO IS EATING THE COMPOST?'
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Weeping Compost Pool
The pool is the colour of a bruise and it is sobbing very quietly. Things float in it that used to be useful. A boot, mostly.
Drink from the pool
It tastes of rain and regret. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Bottle some of it
Somebody will pay for this. Somebody always does. It is usually a hedgehog.
Comfort the pool
You tell it that it is doing great. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, and a bit of its warmth.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: A Patch of Clean Soil
One small patch of the ordinary, honest dirt the Refusemancers love. Restore HP.
The Spore Gauntlet
A tunnel full of drifting spores. Whether you can walk through it depends on how well your deck has been built.
The Strangler Thicket
A tangle of vines that remembers the shape of everything that has ever walked through it.
The Seed Vault
The Refusemancers' seed bank, long since overrun. Some of the seeds are still good. Some of them have opinions.
The Rootbound Golem
A golem with a ribcage of roots and a head of moss. The whole tunnel is part of its body. (Elite)
The Root Tunnels
The roots have grown into the walls, the ceiling, the floor. Whatever lives here has eaten the light.
The Pulsing Wall
The wall pulses with warm, wet light. It is not entirely a wall.
The Heartwood Treant
The oldest tree in the Dump, grown into the Rotheart. It does not recognize you. It does not recognize anything. (Elite)
You sit on the clean soil and breathe. A thread of clear water runs through it, the only clean water you have seen down here.
You breathe in rain and old compost. Beneath you, a worm moves through the loose soil. You let your shoulders drop.
The golem folds into the floor. The tunnel ahead is smoother, warmer, and has a pulse.
You can hear it now: a vast, slow heartbeat, shaking the walls.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The mutant bees have learned farming. What the rot throws away they turn into honey, and what they make they feed back to the rot.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Hive Swarms
When two of its units have died, the hive swarms: two 1/1 Mutant Bees with Flying buzz in.
BZZZZZZZ.
Two 1/1 flying Mutant Bees buzz in.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Something lifts in the Rot Tunnel. Every scrap of Garbage it finds becomes a rep, and every rep becomes Iron.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: Every tendril in the Dump runs to this one place. At its center, wrapped in roots and humming, hangs a seed the size of a fist.
A tag in very tidy handwriting: PROPERTY OF THE PATH-OLOGISTS. LIFE THAT NEVER DIES.
The tendrils feed on the seed, and the seed feeds on grief. Cut them, and the Rotheart will weaken.
But the seed itself will not let go of her. And she will not let go of it.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Heart Roots
Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them. It will hurt, her more than you.
Sever the Heart Roots
The roots shriek and let go. Whatever waits ahead will be weaker for it.
Leave them be
The roots keep pulsing. The Rotheart keeps its strength.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: At the heart of the Rotheart stands Archdruid Compostella, half woman and half tree. Roots run from her arms into the floor and out into every plant in the Dump.
Her eyes are open. They are not hers.
"I... am... THE... DUMP," she says, in many voices at once, sorrowful and enraged. "I am what you throw away. I am what grows back. I am HUNGRY."
Beneath the many voices, one small one: "Please. The tree. I could not let her go."
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Compos: I am what you throw away. I am what grows back. I am HUNGRY.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Roots Spread
At half health the roots spread: two 1/1 Sporelings sprout and her units get +0/+1.
...I am the bin you never empty... nothing leaves... I am HUNGRY...
Two Sporelings sprout; her units get +0/+1.
Please. The Tree.
Near the end a small voice breaks through: her units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
(small) Please. The tree. I could not let her go.
The hungry green falters: her units get -1/-0.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The Rotheart
The corrupted core of the Verdant Dump: a vast, throbbing knot of root and rot, and, at its center, a figure that was once the Archdruid.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::chal: Five cards drift through the spores. If enough of them are infrastructure, they will hold you steady. If not, the spores will sweeten your lungs.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::even: The Whispering Mushrooms
A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. "Stay," they say, in a thousand tiny voices. "Eat.
Listen. Join."
Taste a cap
Listen to what they have to say
Pick a few and sell them
It tastes like rain, soil and tiny, tiny regrets. You feel strangely rested, and your tongue is a little bit blue.
They tell you things. Where the roots run, where the Rot is thin, where the Archdruid used to walk. You hold onto what you can.
It helps. It is not entirely your own thought.
The mushrooms scream, very quietly. You pretend not to hear. A passing trader is delighted, and pays well.
The Pulsing Wall
The wall ahead pulses with a slow, wet heartbeat. A seam runs down the middle. Behind it, warm light.
A voice inside says: "Come. Be held."
Press your hands into the wall
Wait beside it and breathe
Cut a piece of it free
The wall takes your hands, warm and wet. It hurts. Then it does not.
Roots grow along your arms, and, oddly, you feel better rooted in the world.
You breathe in time with the wall, and it quiets. A small bit of warmth moves from the roots into you. You feel mended, and a little ashamed.
It bleeds sap and fury. A glittering stone falls out. It is worth a lot of gold, and a bit of your arm.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::dung: The Archdruid sinks to her knees. The Rotheart lets out a long, shuddering breath, and across the whole Dump a thousand vines unclench.
You hear the vines settle overhead. For a moment, nothing moves beneath your feet.
"...What a terrible dream," Compostella whispers. "The seed. It is still in my roots. It will not die, and I cannot make it."
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::cuts: It is the seed. {villain}'s gift: life that never dies. When the great tree I grew up beneath fell, I could not bear it.
I planted the seed in her place. It took. It has been growing in my grief for ten years. Nothing here rots, because of me.
A seed that never dies isn't a gift. It's a grief that never ends. Let it rot.
Everything I ever loved, I gave back to the soil. Except this one. I could not.
...Then we let it die, together. Hold still. Hold me.
I have never let go of anything so large.
...It is rotting. Honest compost, the first in ten years. Oh. I can hear the soil again.
I can hear the stream. I can hear the goat.
And I can hear her, a little, in all of it. She did not go away. She went into everything.
To grow, I had to let her go. ...I think she has been waiting ten years for me to say so.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.rothe: You see light pour through the splitting Rotheart.
Before you, the purple vines wither. At the heart of the wound, the Archdruid kneels, free and breathing.
You watch wildflowers follow the light outward through the Dump.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::bark: The river's still lovely. Still a nightmare to climb out of. Some things healing can't fix.
Compost sorts itself the normal way again. Slowly. With help. As it should.
The raccoon in the crown says thank you. He also wants your lunch. Still no.
New stairs. Same climb. Worth pausing on, now.
Every terrace a little greener. Even the top one. Especially the top one.
Archdruid's back on her rounds. She waters the weeds too. Says they had a rough decade.
The trees went back to green overnight. Nobody's talking about that either, but happily.
Stall's open! Patched awnings, honest prices, and nothing purple unless you ask for it.
Funny thing. The flowers smell like flowers again. I'd forgotten that was a smell.
The Verdant Dump, healing: the Compost Grange is safe. HP does not come back after battles - sit down to a fresh harvest meal, or walk back down to town.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::ui.e: Leaving the Verdant Dump ends this visit. Town heals you fully; the roaming golems, scarecrows and gulls have calmed down a lot, and so has the garbage.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::sign: THE COMPOST GRANGE
Hub of the Verdant Dump. The Refusemancers handle waste removal and agriculture.
Nothing goes to waste. The Rot has gone. The doors may be opened again.
TODAY'S COMPOST
- Waste removal (by goat)
- Agriculture (by magic)
- Nothing goes to waste. Not even the menu.
- Water things. They like it. They are only plants.
THE ROT: CURED
The plants here are only naturally alive, mostly. The zucchini has been spoken to.
THE ARCHDRUID IS BACK
Archdruid Compostella is recovering. She asks that you not call her "the Rotheart Archdruid" at breakfast.
THE FOREST PATH
To {town}. Moss Mulligan's thorn wall is mulch, and she says sorry again. Vines are just vines now. Still sort your boots.
THE ROTHEART
Source of the sickness, now closed for healing. The vines are only vines. Mostly. Visitors welcome.
NOTE FROM A DRUID
The door is warm because the compost is happy. The compost was always happy. We just forgot what that looked like.
I never thought I'd say it: the Dump is healing. The vines are only vines, the mushrooms are only mushrooms, and the Archdruid is herself again. She is mortified.
Breathe in. Go on. You may breathe deeply now. That smell is honest compost.
This morning Compostella walked straight to the row of royal trees and planted a twelfth. She didn't say why.
She just smiled at you on the way past.
The stream is clean, the fields are calm and the zucchini has gone back to being a zucchini. Thank you. We owe you more than compost.
Though NOBODY has explained who ate the compost. The raccoons have suddenly become excellent listeners.
Granny Gristle, junk-trader! The shed is just a shed again. The turnips are only turnips.
I had a little cry, then I planted a field. Shop's open, dearie. Welcome back to the sane side of farming. Heh!
Shop's open! Day-old turnips. None looking at anybody. Finally, produce that knows when to look away. Heh!
Billie Muckfoot, animal handler! The herd's back, and the goat's eating a sign.
The sign's not eating back. I've never been so happy to see a goat ruin something.
Every animal present and entirely un-mutated. I could cry. I might.
Into a bucket. For the plants.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::free: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. I will help put it right.
