Ten years of the Rot in my roots. It spoke so quietly. It said I was needed. It said the whole world was waiting to grow.
It was my own grief, wearing a seed. Thank you for helping me let it rot.
The Dump will heal. The goat may take longer to trust me. Plant something, child. Anything. It will be glad of you.
You are carrying a loss you cannot name yet, child. When you find its name, do not bury it in a jar. Death is not the end of them.
Let it be the start of something in you.
data/story/refusemancer_story.tres::rule: It looks like the Archdruid. It is still growing. Please do not water.
It used to be the Rot-Idol. Now it is topiary. Please do not water.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: The Groundskeeper's gone. Packed her shears and left for the Capital the moment the Archdruid woke.
She left one pair behind, in a compost heap. Granny Gristle is keeping them. 'Found, not stolen,' she says. Twice.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Hear that? Things rotting properly again. Lovely sound. Means something's about to grow. Heh.
data/story/intro_story.tres::zone.comple: Chancellor Clench is down, Grandmaster Flex is back, and the weights are in the gym. The mills turn at a sensible pace; Gary lifts with a spotter.
The Doppelganger is exposed, the Special Sauce is recalled, and the real Grand Chef is back in her kitchen. The golems guard plates again. Nobody leaves hungry.

Mortimer Grimsby is removed from office, and the vacancy passes by policy to the senior-most applicant on file: Agnes Overdue. The Department of Necrotic Affairs belongs to itself again, and it is terrified by the freedom.
The Rotheart is silent. The vines are only vines again. The Archdruid is herself and deeply apologetic about the barn. The land starts, slowly, to heal.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week! Gerald's number came up. Lovely chap. Brought his own mug.
Agnes stayed, of course. Somebody has to fix the forms. I've put her down for later. Much later. Heh.
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_fragm: Freeing a zone loosens something in your head. Whenever it does, go and tell Elder Maren.
%s: free a zone, then see Elder Maren
Elder Maren's home, up the Gate Road from Crosspath's square
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HOB.barks::0: Checked my book. You're not in it. Not for a good long while. Heh.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-HOB.barks::1: Business has been slow for ten years. Not my fault. Paperwork. Heh.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.in: You're pale. Sit, sit. Something came back to you, didn't it?
Tell me. All of it, however small.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.fr: Light. Four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.
A woman is humming. A tune with no words, rising and falling like breathing.
A hand rests on my head. Gentle. Certain. It smells of lavender and woodsmoke.
Then the light thins, like breath on glass, and I am back.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.af: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days. From the court. Few remember it, and fewer hum it.
Eat some pie. Don't ask me why my eyes are wet.
And look at you. With a zone free, the corruption's grip on the land is slipping, and it is slipping off you with it.
You should be able to carry a second Path now. Go on, try it at the Deck Station.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.1.an: With the first zone free, the corruption smothering your gift has weakened. Your decks may now use two Paths, and dual-Path cards can finally be played.
Decks may now use two Paths.
One zone free and back for pie already. Fine. One slice per zone, dearie. Those are the rules now.
Three roads still shut. I'd go myself, dearie, but I'd arrive next spring.
The square sang last night. Badly. Best thing I've heard in ten years. Don't you dare tell them.
One zone free. Hm. And the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started cheering at night. From the cellar. I am choosing not to ask.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: Someone is sitting on a rock at the mouth of the Forgotten Cave, hood up, sharpening a pencil with a scalpel.
You freed a whole Path. On your own. With a deck you'd known for a week.
Let me see your hands. Steadier. Good. That's the first thing I've been able to tick off in a long time.
Who are you?
Still a friend. Still all I can give you.
I'm not staying in town. The old woman with the shell looks at me like I owe her a pie.
Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls. The woods go quiet when a Path comes loose.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.in: Another one. Don't hide it behind your teacup. Say it.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.fr: White rooms. White light that never changes with the hour.
Glass on every side, and faces behind it in white coats, taking notes.
They never use my name. They call me 'the Subject.' They say 'again.'
I wasn't lost. I was kept.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.2.af: Glass, and coats, and 'again.' So that is where you have been.
You have earned the truth. I have been keeping more from you than I should.
There is a resistance in this kingdom, and I am its contact in {town}. Wren leads it, from a hideout in the Capital.
I wasn't sure I could trust you before. I am now.
Two zones free. The square's louder now. I complain about it every morning and mean none of it.
Halfway, dearie. I'd say I'm proud of you, but then you'd stop trying.
Auntie Alembic keeps asking after you. I tell her you're busy. For once it's even true.
Two zones free. Auntie Alembic has opened her shop on the square, the Alchemist's.
She asks for your leftovers. From her, that is a compliment.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth with two cups of something hot. She hands you one without asking.
Two Paths. People in town are singing again. Badly, but they're singing.
You knew I'd come back here.
You always came back to the same places. Even when you were...
Drink your tea. It's for the shaking.
Even when I was what?
Even when you were someone who couldn't. Ask me something easier.
Favourite colour?
Four of them. Next question.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.3.fr: A throne room at night. Candles guttering, banners with four colors woven as one.
A man in white and gold kneels before the king. Soft voice. Then he stands.
Hands on my shoulders. Two people pushing me behind them, toward the dark.
I know that man's face. I have always known it. {villain}.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.3.af: A man in white and gold, kneeling, and then standing. And a lab with glass on every side.
I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. I founded the study of the Paths, long ago, for the best of reasons.
{villain} took my work and turned it into a cage. My best student kept the lab running for him. And I ran.
I have been hiding here ever since.
That is my secret. Now you hold it, the same as I hold yours.
One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. It's murder on my knees.
Three zones free, dearie. Finish the fourth before my pie goes stale. That gives you about a week.
You walk like somebody with somewhere to be now. I preferred the damp young man. He visited more.
Three zones free. Only one Path left under {villain}'s thumb. I will not say what I'm feeling. I will say it is a lot of feelings.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: She is waiting at the cave mouth again with her hood down, as if she forgot it was up. Her eyes are tired and very sure.
Three. I used to think you were someone else. Someone I lost when we were kids. Now I'm starting to think...
No. Not until I'm certain. Too many people around here say things before they're certain.
You knew me. Before.
I knew a boy who fell on his behind trying to lift a dumbbell, and who ate the frosting off every layer of his cake.
You'd have liked him. He was terrible at hiding things.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.in: There is something in your face today. The look of someone who has been handed a key. Tell me.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.fr: A boy of eleven, in a coat too fine for the cold. Someone calls across a courtyard: '{prince}!'
I turn. A woman's voice. A man's voice. The {royal_house} crest on every door: four signs in a ring.
{prince_full}. The son of the king and queen. Presumed dead.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: {prince}. {prince} {royal_house}. I met a boy once at court, hiding behind his mother's cloak, who asked me why tortoises carry their houses.
I told him, 'So we are never far from home.'
And I knew. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew the moment you walked out of it, and I was too frightened to say so.
Four signs in a ring. The same as on my stick. I have carried it for ten years and told nobody why.
And my lab, my life's work, was used on that boy. Forgive me, if you ever can.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.re: There is nothing to forgive. You gave me a bed and pie when you thought I might be a spy.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: ...Then let us make the kingdom a home again, {prince}.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.in: You have the look of someone who was told something he did not want to hear. {villain}?
Sit. Tell me what he said.
data/story/intro_story.tres::memory.4.af: So he knew you from the first. He told you, and you came to me for the rest.
I knew too, dearie. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew, and I was too frightened to say it.
So hear it from the one who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I am so sorry for what was done to you in my name.
All four Paths free, and {villain} still sitting in his castle. Go and knock, dearie. Loudly.
The roads are open. Even the tortoises use them. I passed one this morning. Barely.
Eat something first. Then the castle. Nobody topples a tyrant well on an empty stomach.
All four Paths are free. {kingdom} is whole again, or nearly. And up in his castle, {villain} is counting what he has left.
Rest. Then we finish this.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cav: The cave mouth is quiet. This time she is standing, cloak fastened, a satchel of four-coloured vials over her shoulder, ready to go somewhere.
All four. The kingdom is breathing again. Like voices through a wall, except the wall is coming down.
There's only the Capital left. Only him.
Come with me.
I'll be at the castle gate when you get there. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
And when it's over, I'll tell you everything. My name first. I promise.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.vi: You touch the stone. It is cold, and then it is not. Far below, something moves that has not moved in years: water, or the memory of it.
...Four streams. One spring. They drank together, once.
...The water went down when they stopped sharing. Not all of it. Listen for what is left.
Two hums answer, faint as a wet finger round a glass. One is on the Verdant Dump's highest terrace, where its river starts to fall.
The other is in the Endless Buffet, by a little pond under the broccoli.
The townsfolk say the well doesn't talk. I'm not going to be the one who tells them.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.to: ...Listen. What is left of the water still hums.
One hum is high in the Verdant Dump, on its highest terrace, where the river starts to fall.
One hum is in the Endless Buffet, by the little gravy pond in the Broccoli Forest.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.fi: At the head of the falls, under a lip of roots and old junk, a thread of water comes up clear. The cleanest water in the Dump starts in its dirtiest corner.
You find a boot in the spring. Clear water slips around its heel. Even here, something finds a way through.
For a blink you see four streams leaving one spring: red, blue, purple and green. This one was green. It fed the fields, and the fields fed everyone.
A whisper, from very far away: 'One stream remembers.'
The pond is gravy, like everything here. Under the gravy, ringed with old stones, is a basin far older than the Buffet: the first stockpot, built round a spring.
You recall the first words of every Gourmand recipe: first, water. Someone has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
For a blink you see four streams leaving one spring. This one was blue. It went into the first pot, and the first pot fed a kingdom.
A whisper, from very far away: 'One stream remembers.'
Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums a little louder. One more stream to find.
Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums like a full kettle. Both streams have answered. Go back to the well.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.to: The well is full. Not of water: of light, every colour of the four Paths at once, turning slowly, like something stirred.
...Both streams remember. Now the spring will see who is asking.
data/story/old_well_story.json::beats.ec: ...I am what is left when the water goes. Every Path's voice, in one throat.
Hold all four, and I will run again. Hold fewer, and I will show you what the others were for.
...Not yet. The spring is patient. It has had ten years of practice.
The light sinks back into the stone. It will rise again when you touch the well.
The light sinks into the stone, and for a moment the well is a mirror. In it you see a spring under the whole kingdom: under the town, under the vault, under everything.
...Once there was one spring. Four peoples drank from it and gave it four names.
They argued about the name for a thousand years. The water did not mind.
Where it rose, they built a town to argue in. Over its source they built a vault, and the four Paths locked it together, so no one Path could own the water.
It ran while the four shared it, and while one house held them together.
Ten years ago the house went quiet. The streams stopped speaking. The spring went down to wait.
The little spring at the end of the old royal tunnel went to dust. This one nearly did.
Good new wells were dug all over the kingdom, clean and straight. The water did not come. It never comes when it is told.
...It does not run for one shape. It runs for many, held together, and it has waited ten years for a hand that can hold all four.
It hums when you touch it. Take a little with you. It remembers the way home.
A well with opinions. I'll take a bottle's worth.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.que: The Old Well remembers a spring that once fed all four Paths. Two hums still answer it, one in the Verdant Dump and one in the Endless Buffet. Find both.
Find what hums in the Verdant Dump
Find what hums in the Endless Buffet
Go back to the Old Well and face what answers
The Dump's highest terrace, where its river starts to fall: something there hums like the well
The little gravy pond in the Buffet's Broccoli Forest: something there hums like the well
The Old Well in {town}, in its yard off the west market street
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.tou: The Old Well hums, low and steady, like a kettle kept warm for whoever comes home.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.con: The Echo duels with all four Paths at once. It is a hard fight. Lose, and nothing is lost: the well will wait.
data/story/old_well_story.json::text.toa: Both streams remember. Go back to the Old Well.

data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: A four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault, four marks set in a ring. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.

data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_i: The stones here were stacked by hands that stopped moving a long time ago.
Something under the cairn is still keeping count of its turns. It has been keeping count since before {villain} came.
Touch it, and it will not stop counting until one of you does.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Re: The stones count. One. Two. The dead are counting with them.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Count Pauses
At half health the dead lose count: their units stand still through their next turn.
The counting stops. Somewhere under the stones, someone has lost their place.
The dead stand still: their units miss their next turn.
The Cairn Remembers
Near the end the dead hesitate: their units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
The dead stop. They look at your hands as if they have seen them before.
The dead hesitate: their units get -1/-0.
data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_v: Whatever was keeping time down there has nothing left to spend it on.
The stones are just stones again. Take what it was guarding.
data/story/intro_story.tres::graveyard_d: Come back when you have more turns to spare than it does.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: A hidden chest in one of Crosspath's odd corners
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Elder Maren says the door under the Old Well has been locked since before she was born. Its key is in a hidden chest somewhere in Crosspath.
Find the hidden chest in Crosspath
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.

The key is in a hidden chest in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one.
You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings, in a ring. Hm. Never mind. I am too old for stairs, dearie. You are not.
The iron hatch beside the well. Go on. Whatever is under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me. Mind the stairs.

Face the Master of the Oldest Trick
core/quests/quest_definitions.gd::_four_: Far away, a great lock ground open. A hidden lever in every Path zone answers a seal somewhere near Crosspath. Find them all.

data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The Wa: Four seals, four Paths, one hand. Show me the hand.

SMOKE BOMB!!! The oldest trick in the book. Page one. I wrote page one.

Body Double

The Last Seal
Near the end the last seal opens: the Warden's units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.

The Warden's units get -1/-0.
Recalibrate

Tick. Damage noted. Tick. Recalibrating.

Recognised

Four colours. One thread. Tick. ...Recognised.

data/story/capital_story.tres::hud.objec: The Capital: the walls are up and the Approved Gate is the only way in. Pass Captain Spotless's entry examination (a card battle), or find another way.
HP does not come back after battles; rifts hurt; the hideout heals. {villain}'s Castle waits at the far end of the city.
Find the hideout through the manhole near the gate. Help the Wrinkles, one quest per Path; seal rifts and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each freed Path mends a broken city service.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.t: Walk back down the road to {town}?
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.b: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The Approved Gate stays open for you, but every roaming officer, inspector and Tidy-Bot will be back next time, and so will the rifts.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.gate.b: Captain Spotless measures you against the Approved Visitor Standard: a hard card battle, his deck fair to nobody. Your HP carries in from the zone and nothing heals in between. Lose, and you wake outside, a little poorer.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.main.b: The great doors stand open, which is worse than closed. Twenty-odd rooms of portraits and good intentions, then {villain} himself. HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines. Your zone's broken-service debuffs apply to every duel.

{villain} is gone. The castle is just a very large, very tidy building now, and the portraits have started to peel. You may walk through it again for the memories (and the gold). HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.main_d: You see your worried face in the gold handles of {villain}'s Castle. Beyond the doors, you smell floor wax and hear someone humming.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.heal_c: Nurse Hesper hands you a cup of the Tea of Dissent. It is strong, bitter and entirely unapproved. HP restored.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.heal_a: You are already at full HP. Nurse Hesper hands you a cup anyway. 'Dissent,' she says, 'is good for the circulation.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.hit::0: Ow! The Capital has hurt you again. (-HP)
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake::: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard that, you notice, is blank on purpose.
'Dragged you in by the collar. Correction fee is yours. Drink. Then we can discuss your habit of arriving unconscious.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake_o: You wake in the dust outside the Approved Gate. A guard leans over you, measuring your height with a long stick.
'Falling in the approved queue area: minor offence. Fine payable. Stand up, citizen. I cannot measure you along the ground.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.chest:: A hidden stash! Someone hid this where {villain}'s inspectors would not look: behind something untidy.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.inside: You are through the walls. Somewhere a loudspeaker clears its throat. You are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.no_tra: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
'Free the Gainlands and we will get the lifts turning.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.shaft:: You drop down the shaft, ride the lift through the dark and climb out somewhere else, smelling of rust.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ladder: You climb the ladder and push the manhole open. The Capital's cold light falls in.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.tunnel: You crawl out through the old tunnel and push the rubble aside. The Outskirts again, and a long way from anybody's approved queue.
You squeeze back down the collapsed shaft and follow the old tunnel in the dark.
You push past rubble and a toppled statue. You find stairs and read an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'
The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints. You walk under them all. It is the best moment you have had all day.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.manhol: You knock three times. The manhole opens to a hand and a tired voice: 'Down you come.'
A manhole by the wall, with a scratch on its lid like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.
A pause. Then the lid lifts and a hand beckons. A voice mutters, 'Wrinkle?' You decide that, yes, you are.
Down a ladder, along a brick tunnel, into a warm room full of mismatched furniture and people who are all, visibly, not ironed.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.deface: You draw a moustache on {villain_title}'s portrait. A small coin drops from the frame: the Wrinkles' bounty for this improvement.
Already improved. He has a moustache now. He looks, for the first time, like a person.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.compla: You post a complaint. A coin drops from a slot with a note: 'Compensation for your inconvenience. Please use it to have less inconvenience.'
You post a complaint. A hatch opens and a warm cup of tea is pushed out, still steaming. 'We value your concern,' says a note. You feel a little better.
You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently. You wait. That appears to have been the whole service.
You post a complaint. A klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.
'Thank you for your feedback,' says the box.
The box rattles. It is full. It has had enough of your feedback for one visit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal::: You set the rift-stone and say the old word: close. The tear shudders, folds in on itself like a letter, and is gone. The air smells of rain. Sealed!
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_g: The rift-stone will not take while the rift's guardian still stands. Whatever it spat out has to go first.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_d: The rift is sealed. Where it was there is a scorch mark and the memory of a very bad idea.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.seal_c: This one is too big. It runs all the way up into the castle. It will have to close when he does.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.pickup: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
A banished compost heap, hiding in a cellar where it was not allowed to be. It is warm. It is alive.
It steams, very slightly, with gratitude. Rescued!
You unwrap a handkerchief and find a worn rubber stamp: FINAL APPROVAL. Someone hid it here, ready for the day it was needed.
An old glass jar with one seed in it. The seed is glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years. It has not given up.
You already took the one lying here.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wheel_: The crew of the first wheel keeps running while you talk, because stopping is not permitted. 'Cardio,' pants a woman, 'is mandatory.' You find the brake lever under a pile of notices.
The wheel groans, slows and stops. The crew sit on the floor and laugh and cry at the same time.
The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.
The wheel winds down. 'We were told,' says a man, 'that this was how you got strong.'
The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.
You pull the lever, break the wheel's rhythm and get them off. They are very small and very proud and they will not stop saying 'Rollo sent you?'.
This crew is free. They are lying on the ground, looking at the sky. It is the best they have felt in ten years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.cable:: You cut the big black cable that feeds the facade's lights from the wheels. A spark; a silence. Far off, the perfect lamps flicker, stutter and come back on: {villain} keeps a very small private generator, just for himself.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.cable_: The cable is cut. The wires twitch occasionally, out of habit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.paste:: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in a bright green foam that smells, fatally, of actual cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.paste_: The dispenser is spoiled and sulking. The foam is still fizzing a little.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot::: With the Stamp of Final Approval pressed to the form, the grave plot's little iron gate unlocks. A line of mourners, who have waited three years outside, file in.
You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot_a: The Pell plot is tended and quiet. Fresh flowers. The family comes every morning now.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.plot_l: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' You have no stamp. Widow Pell said something about a stamp, hidden somewhere in Grave Row.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.patch:: You kneel, scoop a hole with your hands and drop in the seed. You water it with what is left in your flask. Nothing happens, for one long, bad moment.
Then a shoot, as thin as a thread, noses out of the dirt. And another. And a flower, the colour of everything the Capital is not.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.patch_: The patch is green and growing. A bee, which should not exist in the Capital, hovers over it, deciding.
The patch is sick, grey and cracked, and nothing will grow in it without a seed. Old Fern mentioned an old seed in a jar, hidden somewhere in the Reek.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.permit: The clerk behind the window slides you a form. 'For a burial permit, Form 27-B. Please attach Form 27-C (Proof of Grief).'

'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B.' 'Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' 'It is a loop,' you say.
'It is a process,' she says, with fear in her eyes.
'Please take a number.' You take a number. It says 4,112,009.
The sign above the window says NOW SERVING: 3. It has said so for three years.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ward_w: You read: 'Spontaneity Permits: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05, by appointment.' Inside, the clerk sleeps upright, eyes open.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.be: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one small town. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.go: The Gourmands fed and guarded the kingdom. {villain} replaced them with Perfect Nutrient Paste. Real food is gone from the Capital, and so is the comfort it gave.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ne: The Necrocrats looked after the dead and their paperwork. {villain}'s permits locked the dead out of their graves and the paperwork in an endless loop. The dead do not rest, and the things that have died keep coming back.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.re: The Refusemancers took out the kingdom's waste and turned it back into soil. {villain} called composting untidy and hid the garbage behind the facade. Rubbish is piling up, in the streets and in your deck.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ru: The Capital is dark and you can see only a short way.

data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.crea: A Wrinkle is something that does not go away when you press it.
Founded by people {villain} could not iron out. No dues. No forms. No smiling.
Built by all four Paths, together, back when we did that. Six shafts, six streets. (Beefcake wheels power the lifts. No wheels, no lifts.)
2. Eat what you like. 3. Wear a hat of any size.
4. Do not tell anyone where we are.
Another one through the shafts. Sit. I am Wren. I was Royal Archivist, once. Now I keep the records this city is not supposed to have.
Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease. We are the Wrinkles: the people {villain} could not iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea is better.
He is in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he is helping. That is the hard part. Talk to the streets. Each of them holds a piece of him.
Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.
The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.
You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he cannot correct it.
Two pieces of him now. A man who needs to be right. A man who cannot bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.
Three. He is afraid, you know. Not of you.
Of everything that will not obey. A small, sad fear, for a man with so much gold.
All four. I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.
He is a man who made a list of everything he could not control, and made it illegal.
Go and finish it. Gently, if you can. But finish it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.i: Psst. Over here. Fig Sly, purveyor of contraband and curiosities.
Everything on this table is illegal, uneven or both.
Rare cards, good prices, no questions. Well: one question. Would you like a bag? Bags are illegal too.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.r: Back for more? Wise. Rare stock never lasts. Mind the one on the end: it bites.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.hespe: Tea. Strong, bitter, unapproved. Drink while it is still three things the Ministry dislikes.
The rifts? His hold is failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart, and he keeps stitching.
It began the night the boy got out, they say. Nobody says 'boy' where the loudspeakers can hear.
Bleeding again? Sit. I'll pretend to be surprised.
Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.
I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.
They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.
Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.
Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.
I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.
I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.
The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.rollo: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.
Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.
My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.
Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.
The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.marlo: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.
Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste, three times a day. Paste is food the way a form is a hug.
For ten years I've hidden real recipes all over this quarter, so that somebody, somewhere, remembers what food is.
Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.spotl: HALT. I am Captain Spotless. State your height.
No: do not state it. Stand at it. Straighter. Not that straight. APPROVED straight.
Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.
However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.
Do not look nervous. Nervousness is a Violation. (He polishes a button.) Shall we begin?
You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?
You are approved. I have always supported this outcome. Please remember that exact wording.
Please do not tell {villain_title} that I lost. Please do not tell anyone that I lost.
You are... approved. You are retroactively approved.
The Standard is satisfied. The gate opens, by order of the Standard and against my personal feelings.
I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Go through, citizen. In there, try not to be what you are.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.guard: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.
Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.
One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.
Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.
Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.
You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.
Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.
It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.
Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.
Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.
Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.
Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.exit_: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?

data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.patie: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.

I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.
I am improving, they say. I am not sure that is a good thing.

The Pell family plot, at the north end of Grave Row

Widow Pell's husband has sat in the family parlor for three years because his burial permit loops forever. It needs the Stamp of Final Approval, somewhere in Grave Row.
Find the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row
Lay Mr. Pell to rest at the family plot
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Please. A burial permit is all we want: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval.
Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.
The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.
He's at rest? Oh. Oh.
I sat by the plot all morning and didn't say a word. It was the first quiet in three years that wasn't a fear.
Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.
And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.
I don't think he is cruel. I think he simply cannot bear to watch.
Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The energy wheels along the Transit Yards wall
The main power cable, in the Transit Yards
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: The Wheel Never Stops

Free the wheel crews in the Transit Yards
Cut the facade's power cable in the Yards
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.
They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.
Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.
Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.
Haven't heard a quiet yard since the coup. Thank you.
Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.
And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.
Remember that when you meet him. He's always in a hurry... to be loved.
Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Recipe cards hidden around the Hungry Quarter
The paste dispenser, in the Hungry Quarter
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: The Recipe Box
Everyone eats {villain}'s Perfect Nutrient Paste. Chef Marlo's three real recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter. Find them before the inspectors do.
Find Chef Marlo's recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter
Spoil the paste dispenser in the Hungry Quarter
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three of my recipes are hidden in the Hungry Quarter: a bread, a stew, a sauce. Real ones, in my hand, quantities written as 'some'. Find them before the inspectors do.
And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.
Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.
The bread! The stew! The sauce!
Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.
I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.
And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.
He built a whole kingdom of paste because he could not understand what the rest of us were missing.
I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: Banished heaps hide in the Reek's cellars and yards
The Sick Patch in the Reek. Find the jar of old seed first
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::_: Untidy
Composting is outlawed as untidy, and the land is sickening for it. Three banished compost heaps are hiding in the Reek. Rescue them.
Rescue the banished compost heaps in the Reek
Plant the old seed in the Sick Patch
data/story/capital_story.tres::quest.cap: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.
And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.
Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.
It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.
I need to sit down. I need to sit down and smell it.
Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.
Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.
Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.ci: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!
Everything is perfect, and I am so, so pleased about it.
Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.
That is also good. That is the best.
Everything is perfect. Everything is... (a pause, then a whisper) ...please do not tell the Inspector I blinked.
Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.
The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.
I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.
My house is identical to my neighbour's! Is that not wonderful? There is nothing to envy, and nothing to be envied for.
Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.
Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.
Smile! That is all there is to it! Smiling is mandatory, and I am, in my opinion, a very good smiler.
Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.
My cheeks hurt. Please do not tell anyone my cheeks hurt.
The man next door smiled at his wife's funeral. He was remembering her laugh.
(a whisper) They corrected him for a month. He does not remember her laugh now.
The hedge is square! The hedges are all square! I trim the hedge every morning, to make sure it is as square as yesterday's.
The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.
Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.
Once. I wish it would again.
Spontaneity is only for Thursdays! Today is Wednesday! I am almost allowed to be excited!
Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.
I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.
I was corrected for two weeks. (a whisper) I still think about that bird.
Your hat is of an unapproved size, but I will not mention it, because that would be impolite. I am so, so polite. I am the politest person in the Showcase.
Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.
My daughter had a green hat. A little green hat. They said it was a Disagreement.
I do not know where the hat is. I do not know where my daughter is. Everything is perfect.
The Showcase is the best of all possible places! I would not live anywhere else! (looking at the exit) ...I would not be allowed to.
Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.
There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.
{villain_title} is so kind. He loves us all, and he made everything this way, for us. For our own good. (a shake) For our own good.
The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.
I would never look away. I cannot.
He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.
The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.do: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.
It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.
It makes a sound like knocking on a wall.
You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.
They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.
The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.
She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.
You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.
It contains a mop, a bucket and a sign that says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, SMILE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.sp: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!
Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!

Attention, citizens! (a pause) Attention, citizens! (a very long pause) ...the announcement has been completed. Please clap.

Shut down the Paste Works
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: The dispenser is spoiled. Lovely. But the paste comes from somewhere.
The shuttered stall at the south-west corner hums at night. Stalls are not supposed to hum. Open its ration hatch and look. Gently.
The south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch. Whatever is down there, it will be very, very grey.
You shut the vats down? All of them? Then tonight the whole quarter eats something that tastes of something.
Some taste. 'Some' is the best amount.
I have kept one real onion in my apron for ten years. Tonight, I chop it. You may want to stand back. I will be weeping, and not only from the onion.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/quo: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes is timing Rollo's crews. The crews are lying in the sun. She is still timing them.
You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and eleven minutes. I have had the figure framed.
These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent. Now they are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? Unmeasured time.
They're allowed to stop.
Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled. Let me schedule you.
Eighty-one seconds. Faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.
That was not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid.
Flex wants someone... to run the new break schedule... up in the Gainlands. Someone who can count.
Breaks. Scheduled breaks. Mandatory rest, for everyone, forever.
I will hate every minute. I will time every one.
She sits down on the edge of the wheel, stopwatch in her lap, and for the first time in ten years she does not click it.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cli: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation. She has written that down.
Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now. The lawns, the hedges. They grow in whatever direction they like.
I gave her the seed because she was crying. I thought, if nothing ever ends, then nobody ever has to cry again.
That's tidy, isn't it? Isn't that tidy?
Nothing grew there for ten years.
Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Peel from shell. Messy work.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/plu: A peacock in a lavender coat sweeps across the lobby with a ribbon, a pair of golden scissors and a speaking trumpet.
Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. has been freed, a change His Perfection fully supports and in fact arranged!
And you must be the volunteer. A Certificate of Participation. Frame it, or don't. It's been notarized either way.
That's Percival Plume, dear. Deputy Minister of Good News. He drafted the transfer. Every page of it.
And filed it on a Tuesday! Must dash. Ribbons to cut, a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!
He snips the ribbon, which was holding nothing up, and is gone before Agnes can find the right form.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Just measuring. Lot of very tidy people in this city. Tidy is easy to measure.
And the man in the castle?
Him? Hm.
Pencilled in. Heh.
Just measuring. Ran into a peacock earlier, all trumpet and ribbons.
Oh, I've got HIM in pen. Heh. Not soon, mind. I just wanted it to last.

data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PELL.barks::0: He has been in the parlour three years. I still tell him when someone comes to the door.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PELL.barks::1: 27-B needs 27-C. 27-C needs 27-B. I keep both forms beside his chair.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ROLLO.barks::0: Ten years... on the wheel... my calves... have calves.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ROLLO.barks::1: Trained with... the Gainlands wheel crews. They told us... it was cardio.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MARLO.barks::0: Psst. Bread: some flour, a bit of water, enough time. You didn't hear it here.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-MARLO.barks::1: Down here we cook with all the heat and none of the sky. Smell that? Contraband.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FERN.barks::0: Untidy, they call me. Dirt's supposed to be untidy. That's how it works.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-FERN.barks::1: The worms in my hat are unapproved. So am I. We get along.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-CITIZEN.barks::: Everything is perfect! Everything is... (whisper) is it raining? I liked rain.

data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PRIMM.barks::0: I am designing a drain. It will not be perfect. I am learning to let that be.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-PRIMM.barks::1: Good day. I owe you rather more than that. I am told it is a start.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ISLA.barks::0: Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually.
data/npcs/npcs.json::NPC-ISLA.barks::1: Eight years of one front door. Ours gets a new colour every week now.
Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.
Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Going into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow the chalk, not the guards. The guards are worse at drawing.

data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: There's an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That's the point.

Get inside and find the Crease: the manhole near the gate. Knock three times. Not two. Two is rude. Then ask Wren about the tunnels.
