Behind a ration hatch: a real kitchen, a locked pantry and a badger in medals.
A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.
'HALT. These tunnels do not exist. You are standing in nothing. I cannot allow you to have found it.'
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a hatch for rations, is a kitchen. A real one. Copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.
HALT! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
What war? The war on FLAVOUR, son. Every citizen fed the same, at the same time, from the same tap. Perfect discipline.
Marlo says you can't taste it either.
Taste is a weakness. Whisk formation! Golems, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Colone: Ration line, ATTENTION! Whisk formation! Nobody tastes anything!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Enforc: HALT. State your height. No: do not state it. Stand at it.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Battle Rations
At half health Crumb issues paste: he gains 2 Ingredients.
Battle rations! Taste is a weakness. Paste is a strategy!
Crumb gains 2 Ingredients.
Paste Barrage
On his 6th turn the vats open fire: you take 2 damage.
Next turn: Crumb orders a paste barrage (2 damage).
Battle stations! This is not a drill, it is a soufflé!
You take 2 damage.
Inspection
On his 5th turn Spotless inspects your ranks: your strongest ready unit stands to attention (exhausted) and cannot block.
Next turn: Spotless holds an inspection (your strongest unit cannot block).
INSPECTION. Height! Smudges! Smiles at the regulation angle!
Your strongest ready unit stands to attention.
A SMUDGE
Near the end Spotless notices a smudge on himself: his units get -1/-0 while he polishes.
A SMUDGE. Is TREASON. ...It's on me, isn't it.
Spotless polishes: his units get -1/-0.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/cru: Stand down. Stand DOWN. I said... oh, everyone's already lying down. Very well.
The pantry door swings open. Shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, a wheel of cheese with a ration number on it. Somewhere a vat coughs and stops.
I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong. You can't burn paste. You can't oversalt it.
You can't... taste it. I never could, you know. Not since the war that wasn't.
Then you'll learn. The Grand Chef is taking students. She starts everyone the same way: first, water.
...Yes, Chef.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.
'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The great doors swing open, silent and perfectly balanced. Beyond them, a long hall, a red carpet and a smell of floor wax and lemons. Somewhere, a very long way away, someone is humming.
'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'
Four great doors, each in its own Path's colour: red with a dumbbell, gold with a ladle, violet with a notary's seal, green with a seed.
Over each, a brass plate: 'PERFECTED'.
Racks of masks line the walls, each one a face: the Grand Chef, smiling, smiling, smiling. On a clipboard by the door, in a neat hand:
'LAB NOTES: Subject A (the Grand Chef) proved resistant to persuasion. Resolved by substitution. The substitute is cooperative, and does not argue about the sauce.
'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'
A table covered in maps of the Gainlands, with little red pins in every mill and wheel. On a clipboard:
'COUP ORDERS: Remove Grandmaster Flex. Remove his weights, his protein, his gymnasium. Observe.
'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'
Shelves of paper to the ceiling, every sheet stamped. On the top of the pile, a single form:
'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain_title}. Reviewed. Approved.
Filed. VALID. NOTE: the Necrocrats will obey this, because it is their nature to obey a valid form.
I did not need to force anyone. I needed only to be correct.'
In the middle of the greenhouse, under a glass dome, a single seed sprouts, glowing sickly green. A label on the pot:
'THE SEED: Nature is untidy. Nature is inefficient. Nature disagrees with itself.
A seed, properly corrupted, can be made to agree with me. Plant in the Archdruid. Observe.
NOTE: it will spread. What grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: The castle gate is white and gold and perfectly symmetrical. In its shadow, hood up, stands the woman who pulled you out of the woods, as if she was always going to be here.
Don't look so surprised. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located!
Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse. Not toward you. Toward her.
Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume. Former junior Path-ologist. Absent without leave. Removed one item of laboratory property, which has been walking about ever since.
Don't fret, Miss Vey. Your father is very understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen. The long way.
Don't follow me, {wanderer}! Get to the top. That's the only way any of this ends.
They are through a side door before you reach it. The door has no handle on this side. Of course it doesn't.
{rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}. I never even asked.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Great Doors
Solid gold, ten metres tall, polished until you can see your own worried face in them. They open before you touch them. That is the worst part.
The Great Hall
A hall the length of a street, and not one speck of dust. Guards stand at attention every ten paces, each one exactly the same height. (A battle.)
The Portrait Gallery
Thousands of portraits of one man, in order. Each is a little taller, a little straighter, a little more perfect than the last. A story event.
The Curator's Rounds
You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)
The Forgotten Alcove
A side door behind a very large frame: a small alcove where the old portraits went when they were replaced. A dead end with a prize, then back to the gallery.
The Mirror Knight
A knight made entirely of mirror plates, each of them showing only one face. It moves exactly like you. Then it stops doing that. (A battle.)
The Hall of Mirrors
A hall of mirrors that reflect only him. A deck challenge: how well do you lead with your own face?
The One Honest Mirror
A small, dusty mirror in a closet, hung by someone who had to hide it. It shows whoever is standing in front of it. A dead end with a story.
The Quiet Room
A room of mirrors where, for once, nobody is reflected at all: they have been turned to face the wall. Rest here. Restore HP.
The Desk of Correction
A long brass desk, a stamp and a form: 'FORM OF CORRECTION'. A deck challenge: do you have the bodies to fill the form?
The Ministry Clerk
You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)
The Chief Corrector
The head of the Ministry of Correction: white gloves, kind eyes, a ruler. She is very, very gentle. That is what makes it frightening. (Elite)
The Corrected
A long ward behind the Ministry where citizens who were 'corrected' are kept. A dead end with a story, then back to the corridor.
The Hall of the Four Wings
A circular hall with four doors, one for each Path. Each wing is a dead end: a place where he 'perfected' that Path. Visit any, all or none; then take the corridors on.
The Gourmand Wing: The Laboratory
The doppelganger's laboratory: vats of Special Sauce, rows of masks, one very worried technician. (A battle, then lab notes.)
The Beefcake Wing: The War Room
A war room full of maps, flags and one very large, very empty throne: the place where the coup was planned. (A battle, then the orders.)
The Necrocrat Wing: The Notary's Office
A tall office of notarized, filed and countersigned paper: the authorization that took the Necrocrats. (A battle, then the paperwork.)
The Refusemancer Wing: The Greenhouse
A glass greenhouse where something glowing and green grows in a single pot. The Rot began here. (A battle, then the seed.)
The Servants' Corridor
A narrow back corridor where the castle's servants work, silent and very fast, in matching grey. They do not smile. They have stopped. (A battle.)
The Grand Staircase
You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
The Wing Vault
Where the two ways round the wings meet: a small vault of confiscated things. Treasure.
The old portraits lean against the wall, face to the plaster. Behind the last one: a small bag someone left. 'In case anyone comes looking for the real one,' says a note. You take it and go back.
You sit on the floor between mirrors that show only plaster. It is, for a few minutes, the most peaceful room in the Capital. Somebody has left a mug of tea and a biscuit.
The biscuit is a little crooked. You eat it.
The Chief Corrector sits down on her own chair, very carefully, and lays her ruler on the desk. 'I corrected eleven thousand,' she says.
'I never once asked what was wrong with them. Please. The door on the left. Go and look.'
You tear the last page off the clipboard. Under the neat hand, in the margin, in a small shaking one: 'He did not look at the faces. He never looked at the faces.'
You fold it into your pocket and go back.
In the margin of the orders, in a smaller, shakier hand: 'He was not weak. We took everything from him and he got stronger. I do not understand it.'
'I have asked the champions to be weak. They will not.' You fold the orders and go back.
The Wraith's last words, as it folds: 'The authorization is valid.' Then, very quietly: 'It was never right.'
You take the form. It can be revoked, you suspect, on a technicality. You go back.
The dome is cracked. The glowing seed lies in the dirt and is, for a moment, just a seed. In the label's margin, in a smaller hand: 'She was grieving. I told myself that made it a kindness.'
You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Grand Foyer
A portrait of a smiling ruler fills the wall. The floor is so polished you can see yourself, and he is standing behind you in every reflection.
Study the portrait
The smile never changes. Neither, you realise, does anything else here. It is strangely restful.
Pocket a gilded candlestick
Heavier than it looks, worth more than it should be, and covered in your fingerprints in a building that remembers fingerprints.
Count the reflections
There is always one more than there should be. You wave. He waves second. You are, for a moment, a little less afraid of him.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Reflection
At half health a reflection steps out of the glass: a 1/1 Reflection joins (Polished makes it 4/2).
Every mirror in this hall agrees with His Perfection. So does this one.
A Reflection steps out of the glass.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The sign is older than the rest of the castle. It is painted by hand. Under it, in different ink, someone has written: 'He meant well.'
A lectern in the middle of a round room, a book open on it, a pen beside the book. The ink on the last page is still wet. He wrote this today.
The Archive Door
A tall oak door with a brass sign: 'ARCHIVE OF GOOD INTENTIONS'. A warden stands in front, arms folded. (A battle.)
The Early Journals
Shelves of journals in a young man's handwriting: the years before the throne. A story event.
The Reading Room
A quiet reading room, a lamp, a chair. Someone used to read here. Rest and restore HP.
The Blueprint Vault
A side vault of blueprints: the sound reforms he drew up before it all went wrong. A dead end with a prize, then back to the reading room.
The Escalation Shelf
A single long shelf where the reforms are filed in order. Each is a little bigger than the last. A deck challenge: can your deck keep its footing?
The Archive Automaton
A tall brass automaton that files, stamps and shelves. It has been told the archive is complete. It is very sure. (Elite)
The Last Journal
A single book on a stand, still open. The last page is still wet. A story event: the moment you see him as he sees himself.
The Model Warden
The last guard before the Chamber of the Model: a warden whose job is to keep everyone away from the table. (Elite)
You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.
Plans for wells. Plans for a school lunch. Plans for a bridge that was actually built.
You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.
The Warden steps aside. Through the doors: a huge round room, a vaulted ceiling and, on a table the size of a house, a perfect miniature of the whole kingdom.
Somebody is bending over it, moving a tiny house one centimetre to the left.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Hold the Stair
At half health the guard plants his feet: the next 3 damage to him is absorbed.
No one climbs. The stair has been polished. By seventeen people.
The guard absorbs the next 3 damage.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Chamber of the Model is round and domed, and in its centre stands a table the size of a house: a perfect miniature of {kingdom}.
Roads, rivers, four districts, a hundred thousand tiny houses. Every one of them is exactly where he wants it.
A man in a pressed grey coat and a thin gold circlet stands with his back to you, moving a tiny cottage one centimetre to the left with a pair of tweezers.
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Primm/: Do mind the floor. It has just been polished, by seventeen people, whom I thank daily, in writing.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Out of Alignment
At half health Primm corrects the room: the next 2 damage to him is absorbed.
Do hold still. You are very slightly out of alignment. There. Better.
Primm absorbs the next 2 damage.
Every Mirror Agrees
On his 5th turn a polished reflection steps out to stand with him: a 2/2 Reflection.
Next turn: a reflection steps out of the mirrors.
Every mirror in this castle agrees with me. I find that very restful.
A 2/2 Polished Reflection steps out.
I Only Wanted It to Be Nice
Near the end Primm comes apart: his units get -1/-0 for the rest of the fight.
I only wanted it to be nice. For everyone. For their own good.
Primm's units get -1/-0.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Scale Model Chamber
A giant model of the whole kingdom, and the man who rearranges it by hand. {villain_title}, {villain}. (Boss: three phases)
data/story/capital_story.tres::challenge: Every mirror shows only him. They turn to look at you and, for a moment, one of them hesitates. Reveal cards until the first unit: if its attack is 3 or more, a mirror will let you through (and show you, briefly, yourself).
If not, they will look through you and it will hurt.

A FORM OF CORRECTION asks for a list of bodies: names, numbers and heights. Five cards are revealed; if at least two are units, you have enough people on your form to get past the desk. If not, the stamp comes down.

Every reform on the shelf is bigger than the last: school lunches, lunch rules, lunch inspectors, inspector rules. Five cards fall off; if at least two are infrastructure, your deck holds. If not, the shelf comes down on you.
data/story/capital_story.tres::event.pc_: The Improved Portraits
Thousands of portraits of one man, one a year. In the first he is a thin young clerk, anxious and kind, smiling at nothing in particular.
Each one is a little straighter, a little taller. By the last he is eleven feet tall, with no wrinkles and a smile that does not move. Under each: 'IMPROVED.'
Study them closely, from the first to the last
Look away and breathe
Take a gold frame off the wall and sell it
You look at them all, in order. The anxious clerk grows steadily less anxious, and steadily less there. You find the exact portrait where it happens: the tenth.
In the ninth he looks so tired, and so sincere. You will not forget it. You see through the frame.
You look at your feet. The carpet is red, and a little worn in the middle. That, at least, is honest. You feel a little steadier.
The frame comes off with a squeal. Somewhere an alarm goes off, very politely: 'Please do not remove the improvements.' A hand-sized portrait falls and cuts your hand. The frame is worth a lot.
The One Honest Mirror
In the broom cupboard, behind a bucket, hangs a small, cracked mirror. A note taped to it: 'FOR THE WRINKLES. IT SHOWS WHOEVER STANDS IN FRONT OF IT. WE LOST A MAN FOR THIS MIRROR.'
You step in front of it and, for the first time in this castle, you see yourself.
Stand and look for a while
Take the mirror's frame; it is quite valuable
Your face. Tired, dusty, crooked, entirely your own. It is the most welcome thing in the castle.
You stand there until you feel like yourself again, and a little more.
You remove the old gold frame. The mirror remains hanging; you can still see yourself. The gold will sell for a good price.
The Corrected
A long white ward. Fifty beds. In each, a citizen in a grey gown with a small, fixed smile, looking at nothing.
A nurse moves among them, adjusting each smile by a few degrees. One man has been smiling at the ceiling for three years. A woman in the corner has forgotten the name of her own daughter.
One of them whispers to you as you pass: 'I smiled at a funeral.'
Sit with them and listen
Free the nearest bed and help them out
Take the ward's record book as proof
You sit by the bed and listen, for as long as it takes. It takes a long time. They tell you their names.
You listen to what they smiled at: a funeral, a wedding, a bird. When you rise, you repeat their names to yourself.
You undo the straps and help a man to his feet. He weeps and laughs and falls over, and cannot remember how to frown. A nurse hits an alarm.
You carry him out through a window. He is heavier than you expected. It costs you a little. It costs him far more.
He says: 'Thank you.' It is the first thing he has said in three years.
The record book lists every citizen corrected, their offence and the angle of their smile on admission. It is eleven thousand pages long. You will not need to read it all.
The first page is enough. Somebody will pay for this book. Somebody, one day, will read it aloud.
The Hall of the Four Wings
Four great doors in four Path colours, and over each a brass plate: PERFECTED. Behind each, you can hear nothing at all. A fifth and sixth way lead on: the servants' corridor and the grand staircase.
You could visit all four wings, or none. Each wing is a dead end, and each one will tell you how he did it.
Rest on the bench in the hall
Take the coins from the collection plate by the door
You sit on a long bench under a brass plate and breathe. The doors do not open. Nothing in the hall moves, and everything in it seems to be listening. After a time you feel steadier.
You find the brass collection plate bolted to the wall, marked for {villain_title}. You take the coins.
You close your hand around the money and leave the empty plate.
The Grand Staircase
A staircase of five hundred steps, every one exactly the same height, and at the top a very large clock.
Halfway up, a servants' door stands ajar: through it, a narrow plain stair with worn steps. Nobody has ever climbed the grand staircase for pleasure.
Climb the grand staircase, step by identical step
Sit on a step and rest
Take the servants' stair
Five hundred identical steps. By the three hundredth you are trembling; by the four hundredth you want to scream.
You find a pot of coins on the top landing, left as a tip by the last climber. You rub your legs and pocket it.
You sit on step two hundred and fifty, and look up at the very large clock. It has no hands. It has only a plate that says 'ON TIME'.
You sit there for as long as you like. Nobody comes to correct you.
The servants' stair is steep and narrow and wonderfully uneven. Every step is a different height. A cook has left a little shelf of bread and a pipe.
You eat and climb and feel, curiously, much better about the whole world.
The Early Journals
A wall of journals in a young man's neat handwriting, each one dated. 'Year 1: Wells. Half the lower city has to walk two miles for clean water.
I have drawn up plans for six new ones. The Council has approved them. I did not sleep. It was wonderful.'
'Year 3: School lunches. A child asked me why the soup was warm. I said, so that you can eat it.
She said, that is the best idea anyone has ever had. I put it in a frame.'
You keep reading. Page after page describes work that helped people.
Read the first journals, all the way through
Close the book and sit with it for a moment
You read until the light changes. Wells, schools, bridges, lamps: he built a hundred good things, and he loved every one.
You read the last plan twice. You recognise the care in it. You close the journal gently.
You close the book and rest your hand on the cover. It is warm, as if someone had just put it down. You breathe, and wait until your hands are steady.
The Last Journal
The last page, in a neat hand, the ink still wet: 'Today I corrected eleven more. They cried, which is understandable. They do not yet see it.
In ten years' time they will thank me. In a hundred, they will not remember there was anything to thank me for. That is the point. That is how you know it has worked.
I am so tired. I do not think anyone has ever tried so hard to be kind. I only wish somebody would say so.'
Read it all again, and let it settle
Close the journal and steady yourself
You read it twice. He believes every word: that each portrait and each rule is a gift, that nobody has ever tried so hard to be kind.
He is not lying. That is the worst of it. You understand him a little, and you understand exactly what you will have to do.
You close the book softly. Whatever is in the next room, it is not a monster. It is a man who needed to be right, and made the whole world pay for it.
You breathe in, and out, and you go on.
Ah. A visitor. Do come in.
Mind the floor: it has just been polished, by seventeen people, whom I thank daily, in writing.
I am {villain_title}, {villain}: Minister of Improvements, Steward of the Throne, Protector of {kingdom}.
You have walked the whole length of my castle. You have, I notice, scuffed it.
I've walked a long way. Everyone I met was afraid of you.
Afraid? Of what? Of order?
Of comfort? Of being safe? I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules.
Every one of them has a number. I can account for every citizen. Nobody need be overlooked.
Ten years I have been mending this kingdom. Ten years, and still you come, with your different hats and your different opinions, to undo the only good thing anyone has ever done.
I am afraid I shall have to correct you.
Please remain still. I know how to put this right.
Why... why will they not all be three? It is a perfectly good number.
Every unit, equal, in every way. Why must some of them be five? Why must anything be five?
People are different. You know that.
You took ten years from me. Whatever you took, it was not the part that matters, and strength is not control.
People are different. You know that.
You took ten years from me. I don't know everything you took. I know it wasn't the part that matters.
Then they must be made the same. For their own good. Do you not see?
You are not listening. Nobody ever listens. (a breath) Very well. If you will not follow my rules, I shall use yours.
Everything you can do, I can do. I have had ten years of practice with it.
Let us see how you like fighting yourself.
Your cards. Your plays. Your own deck, in my hands.
And you still beat me. How?
You copied my cards. What I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
My name is mine to sign. You don't get to decide who I am.
You copied my cards. What I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
I'm not your subject. You don't get to decide who I am.
You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them.
I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
That is not true. I made the wells. I made the roads.
I made... (he stops.) I made a list of things other people had already built, and I put my name on it.
NO. No, no, no. The rules are PERFECT.
The rules ARE perfect. If the rules are not perfect then I have been... then I have been...
Everything is coming apart. Why is everything coming apart? I only wanted it to be nice!
data/story/capital_story.tres::boss.phas: Every unit, yours and his, is a 3/3. You may play at most two non-infrastructure cards a turn. (Two is the perfect number.)
His deck is a copy of yours, and he draws an extra card each turn. He can only imitate; he has never created anything.
His units get +1/+1 and he draws an extra card each turn, but he loses 1 HP at the start of each of his turns. The rules he wrote are breaking down.
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.beef: You see Grandmaster Flex step from behind a pillar, unwinding a bandage from his arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
'The heart and the mind, son. You brought both. We are with you.' (Grandmaster Flex's Heart: Beefcake units get +1 power, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.gour: You see the Grand Chef in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? Let me help.'
'Ten years of sauce that tasted of nothing. Let us feed this kingdom something real.' (The Grand Chef's Feast: Gourmand units get +1 defense, life gain is stronger, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.necr: Agnes Overdue floats forward with her enormous ribboned stack of denied appeals. 'I have found a technicality, dear,' she says, and stamps it with the department seal.
'The rules must answer for him too.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.refu: Archdruid Compostella kneels and presses a palm to the marble. A small green shoot pushes up through the polish.
'To grow, you have to let things go, child. Even him. Especially him.' (Compostella's Roots: Refusemancer units get +2 defense, and you gain 2 max HP.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::boon.none: Nobody stands beside you. The Paths are not free yet: their leaders are still behind wheels, behind sauce and behind paperwork. You step into the chamber alone.
(Free the Paths and their leaders will stand with you.)
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.
{villain} sits among them, small, in his pressed grey coat, and does not move for a long time.
...It is over. The rules were not enough.
I did it for them. I did it for the people. You do see that?
You must see that. Every rule, every portrait, every hat: so that nobody would ever be afraid again. So that nobody would ever be wrong.
You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm not burying that in a jar. I'm letting it go.
You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting go. I won't keep living in what you did.
...(a long silence)... I made them smile. I made them all smile.
And they smiled, and they smiled, and I looked at their faces, and I thought: they look like me. And I was so happy.
It was the mirrors. Wasn't it. I wanted a world where nothing could surprise me.
And I forgot that a world where nothing surprises you is a world with nobody else in it.
I'm not going to correct you. That was your way. Start smaller. Say sorry to one person.
One? I corrected eleven thousand. Where would I even begin? I cannot remember a single one of their names.
Take the crown. No: leave it. No: take it.
It is very heavy. It was always very heavy. And tell the Wrinkles... tell them I am sorry about the hats.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.primm: You hear the mirrors crack one by one. For the first time in ten years, {villain} sees himself in them.
Above the small kingdom, you see a tired man kneeling without his crown or his perfect smile.
You stand in the light pouring through the broken glass.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Doppelganger's Lab Notes
A lab table of food notes: a shapeshifter's recipe for becoming a Grand Chef, with an entire page on how to smile like her. The margins are full of practice smiles.
Read the notes
It explains everything, including why the sauce tastes of nothing. There is no Grand Chef in here, only a very good understudy.
Take the samples
Somebody downstairs will pay for them. Nobody upstairs will miss them. That is the whole plan.
Practise the smile in the mirror
It is perfect. It is horrifying. Your face stays like that for a while, and the guards leave you alone.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: The Necrocrat wing's archive is filing from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
MEMO. To: His Perfection. From: P. Plume. Re: the leak in the lab. The junior Path-ologist has been returned to the Path-ology Lab beneath the forest, to her father. Handled. Promotion?
Ah! You found my memo. Isn't it well written? I used the active voice.
Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News. I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, filed it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land.
Beneath the forest where you... oh, I shouldn't have said that. Never mind. Great news: your visit is being declined!
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::Perciv: Smile, please! This fight is being broadcast, and you are losing it beautifully.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Positive Spin
At half health Plume announces that he is fine: he heals 2.
Great news, citizens! I have been approved to feel fine!
Plume heals 2.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/pc_: This is a setback. A temporary, fully reversible, not-at-all-my-fault setback.
I'll draft a statement. 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes. Bravely.
He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket. Beneath the forest. Her father.
data/story/capital_story.tres::dungeon.p: The Path-ologists' records are pinned to every door. 'SUBJECT 1, the Royal Asset. Drain cycle 3,114.
Power stable, routed to the Throne. {villain}'s hold depends on it. Do not allow the Subject to leave.'
You read the word Subject until it stops being a word.
The oldest notes, at the far end, are in a different hand: careful, rounded, familiar. 'Observation, Year 1. The child is not a specimen. He asks for his mother. I am leaving the lab. M.'
You have seen that handwriting on a pie recipe.
The Correction Ward
A long ward of white cells. Free the prisoners for a boon, and read what the Path-ologists wrote.
A single portrait hangs in a gilt frame, lit like a shrine: a royal family of three.
The king and the queen have been painted over in white, so carefully that every brushstroke runs the same way. Only the boy between them was left untouched.
A small card on the frame, in a neat hand: 'KEPT FOR REFERENCE.' The boy has your face.
You stand there a long time. Your throat has closed, and you cannot say why.
{villain}'s Private Gallery
A small gallery behind a mirror, which nobody is allowed to clean. A dead end with a prize.
Behind the frame, a hidden hatch holds a small bag. You take it, and you do not look back at the portrait, because if you do you will not be able to leave.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: The Hour Strikes
On its 4th turn the clock strikes: your two strongest ready units are exhausted and cannot block that turn.
Next turn: the hour strikes (your two strongest units cannot block).
BONG. The hour has been standardized. All movement will now cease.
The hour strikes: your two strongest ready units are exhausted.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Garden of Uniform Flowers
A thousand identical flowers stand in identical rows. You count them twice. One of them is, very slightly, a different shade of yellow.
Pick the odd one out
It tastes of dandelion. It feels like the first honest thing in the castle.
Pick a handful of the rest
They wilt in your hand and leave behind a few coins, which is more than they should have been able to do.
Plant something crooked
You press a bent stem into the soil. The gardener will find it tomorrow and have to rethink everything. You walk on, lighter.
data/story/capital_story.tres::hud.objec: The Capital is free. The facade is down, the rifts are closed and the citizens are saying whatever they like, mostly to each other. The Crease is open to everybody.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ui.exit.b: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. Nobody will ask for your exit permit. Nobody has a permit machine. The road is just a road.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.main_d: The doors of {villain}'s Castle stand open. The gold is flaking. A pigeon has built a nest in the crown above the lintel and nobody has asked it for a permit.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.wake.f: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard. It says 'NOTES', and then, in small letters, 'finally'.
'Fell over. We rolled you in. Fee is yours. Drink the tea while it is hot; freedom hasn't changed that part.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.be: The lights are back on: the street lamps burn, the lifts run, the tunnels are open again, and the Beefcakes' wheels, free at last, turn for everyone.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.go: The food stalls have reopened: awnings, steam, lanterns, real food. Healing items work again, and the stomachs of the Capital are not quite so empty.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.ne: The cemetery is calm: graves are tended, the permit loop has been broken, and the dead are finally allowed to lie down.
data/story/capital_story.tres::debuff.re: The heaps are smaller and greener. Things are being composted again and the Reek smells, very faintly, of flowers.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.gate: Everybody is welcome. Conditions: none. Please do not feed the pigeons.
1. Be of whatever height you are.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.faca: Now: some houses. A very tidy lawn. A lot of citizens who would like to go home.
Somebody has crossed out BY PERMIT and written BY SURPRISE.
(somebody has written 'when you feel like it' underneath, in small neat letters)
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.cast: Under new management. The new management is: all of us, arguing.
The tears are sealed. The pigeons have moved in. The pigeons are staying.
data/story/capital_story.tres::sign.plaz: Proceed however you like. There is a very large statue; it is lying down.
You did it. Sit. I am Wren: Royal Archivist, and for ten years the only honest record in this city.
The Crease is just a cellar now. We are keeping it anyway, for the stories.
Thank you. I mean that more than I have ever meant a footnote.
The kingdom is mending, one argument at a time. It is dreadfully inefficient. I have never been happier. Take your time.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.i: Fig Sly, formerly purveyor of contraband. Now: purveyor of things. It is a much less exciting job.
The margins are better. Take a look.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.fig.r: Still selling. Nobody arrests me. It is horrible. I miss the thrill.
Old Fern. Composter. Allowed to say it out loud now.
The patch came in, the heaps are steaming and nobody's hit me in a week. Untidy and proud.
Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Waste of water when I could be watering the patch. Come back any time.
Widow Pell. My husband is at rest. I visit him every morning.
Thank you. I will never say it enough, so I keep saying it.
We visit every morning. I tell him about the people who helped us. I tell him about you.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.rollo: Rollo Spokes. The wheels are slow, and the crews are sitting in the sun, lifting nothing. Best I've ever seen them look.
We're lifting again. Real things. On purpose. Come and watch the crews. Bring a snack.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.marlo: Chef Marlo. Chef. Say it with me. The stalls are open and the food is real.
Flour on the ceiling. Food on the plates. Everything in its proper place, at last.
Come and eat. 'Some' of everything. If you ask how much, I shall have to demonstrate.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.spotl: I do not measure anyone any more. I just stand here. Yesterday a man walked by at exactly the approved height, and I wept.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.patie: Citizen... no. My name is Aldous.
I smile now, when I want. It comes out crooked. My wife says it is the best thing she has ever seen.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.ci: Good day! A good day! The weather is whatever it wants!
I do not know the hat size and I do not care! It is wonderful to be alive.
A hat of any size. I keep looking up, trying to decide.
I blinked just now. Twice. Nobody came.
The bakery is painted on. We want a real one. None of us knows how to bake yet. Anyone can volunteer to be the first to burn a loaf.
My name is Berta. I had forgotten. It was on the tip of my tongue for ten years.
Berta. Berta. Berta. It is a very good name.
My house is different from my neighbour's now. He has painted his purple. I am furious. I am so happy to be furious.
I painted my door green. Do you like it? Please say no, so I can have an argument.
I go behind the house and look at the wall, still. It is a good wall. It is just a wall.
I smiled at a funeral yesterday. Nobody corrected me. It was a good funeral.
I cried and smiled and it was exactly right.
My cheeks do not hurt any more. My cheeks are mine.
I will not smile at all today if I do not want to. I am enjoying it.
The hedge is round. I kept trimming the corners, and then I wondered why I wanted corners.
Visitors come! Real ones! They are mostly confused, but they come.
The loudspeaker is silent. I stood under it for an hour. I said my name aloud, myself.
Spontaneity every day! I don't know what comes next! I can hardly wait!
I said hello to the bird again. I have named the bird Thursday.
I do not know what to do on a Thursday, now it is all of them.
My daughter came home. With the little green hat. I have never seen a hat I loved more.
Every hat size! All of them! Come and see the hats!
May I be honest? Your hat is awful. Thank you for wearing it.
I opened the door at the back. It was raining. I stood in it for an hour.
The Showcase is not the best of all places. It is a place. It is mine. It is a good place.
I am going to go somewhere else. Just to see. Then I will come back, if I want.
He was not kind. He was afraid. I think both can be true.
I am not sure I forgive him. I am not sure I need to.
The portraits are coming down. There is a lot of wall behind them. Nobody knows what to put there.
He is gone. I looked away. I looked away for a whole minute. It was a very long minute.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.do: The front door is still painted on. Someone has written under the knocker: 'Come round the back, we have a kettle.'
The painted window now has a real curtain, hung over it by a citizen who wanted one. The family in the painting has acquired a moustache.
The door has a handle now, and the house has an inside: two chairs, a table, a tea tray. The paintbrush has been left on the ladder, for good.
The closet is a closet. The sign says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SMILE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::facade.sp: Attention, citizens. (a cough) This is a loudspeaker. Nobody is on the other end.
Please do whatever you like. That is all.
Attention, citizens. A reminder: you do not have to smile. (a pause) Also: you may smile. We are very easy.
Attention, citizens. A pigeon is using the loudspeaker. Please stand by.
Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.
Attention, citizens. He was afraid, and we were afraid of him. Please be gentle with yourselves.
Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.
Attention, citizens. The exits are open. The entrances are open.
The walls are still walls. Please do not run into them.
Attention, citizens. All is not well. It will be.
It is a lot of work. Thank you for helping.
Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank them.
They are in the cellar. There is tea.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.guard: I used to measure people. Now I just look at them. A man walked past yesterday who was nine feet tall and I said 'good morning'.
I am not myself. I am much better.
Come in, come in. Bring any height.
Queue management. There is no queue any more. I am standing here out of habit.
Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.
Still no queue. I am doing very well.
Exit control. You may leave whenever you like. I am just standing here. It is a very open exit.
Exit control. Goodbye. Come back. Goodbye.
Exit control. This is an exit. It is also an entrance. It is, from every angle, a door.
A door. A good door.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.exit_: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for leaving?
...I was never going to read the answers. Please go and have a nice day.
data/story/capital_story.tres::npc.hespe: Still unapproved. Nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to my tea.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/mar: Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, by way of a pigeon who was very rude about it.
Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate. The one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}.
I knew that face the day you walked in here. Her father worked in my laboratory, once. I never trusted her for a minute.
I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.
Back where she came from, I expect. Somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open. Not yet.
Eat. You'll want your strength for when it opens.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/wre: We saw them take her at the gate. Four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get close.
The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we'll know.
Her name goes in the true record. Whatever else happens.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.be: The Model Falls
You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.
In the gallery a portrait slips off its hook and lands face-up. For the first time in ten years, nobody picks it up.
The Facade Falls
In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.
Shopfronts topple. Hedges wilt into their own shapes. The loudspeakers cough once and go quiet.
Behind the facade: houses, lawns and people, all of them a bit crooked. A child paints the new sign at the gate: PATHORDIA.
The Rifts Close
Across the Capital the rifts fold up like letters. In the Reek, the Sick Patch is a flower bed.
In Grave Row, a family walks slowly to a quiet plot and stays. In the Transit Yards the wheels slow, and slow, and stop, and the crews lie in the sun.
In the Hungry Quarter, somebody lights a stove.
The Wrinkles
The Wrinkles climb up out of the Crease, blinking, into a light they had forgotten. Wren carries the true records under her arm. Nurse Hesper has brought the tea.
You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.
The Paths Meet
And the Paths come home. Grandmaster Flex, the Grand Chef, Agnes Overdue and Archdruid Compostella meet in the plaza and look at one another for the first time in ten years.
You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.
Nobody agrees on anything. It is the happiest sound the Capital has ever heard.
Together
{villain} demanded one way for everyone. It was never what made the kingdom strong.
You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.
The point was never to be the same. The point was the argument. Different Paths, working together.
The New Decree
A new decree appears on the plaza wall of {pathordia}, in four different handwritings. It reads: DIFFERENT PATHS MAY MIX AGAIN.
You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.cr: A game about a kingdom that was strong because it was not the same.
Art: Kenney, KayKit, game-icons.net and friends (see CREDITS.md)
{villain}'s rule is over. The voices of the kingdom remain.
For everyone who waited to be heard.
For everyone learning to choose again.
The Paths will be back, in some other order.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.re: You are back in {pathordia}. It is mostly the same streets, but it sounds quite different: people are shouting at each other cheerfully, in every direction.
Wren sits on the edge of the fountain with a ledger on her knee, writing the title of the first honest page: THE TRUE RECORD, VOLUME ONE.
data/story/capital_story.tres::fx.ending: The Capital is free. The postgame begins: decks of three or more Paths are now allowed.
data/story/capital_story.tres::freed_npc: Breathe in. Hold. ...Feel that? That is a city with nowhere it has to be.
Rollo's crews are lying in the sun. I told them rest is a rep. They believed me. Heart and mind, son. You used both.
The sauce is gone from every stove in the kingdom. Real onions again. I have not wept so much since I was a girl.
You did something worth signing, you know. Now sit. Eat. Eat a mess.
Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.
I think I am going to cry. I have wanted to for a very long time.
Look at this crack in the marble. Something is growing out of it.
I am going to let it. It has earned the right. So have you, child.
...You do not even know, do you? Look at you. You have walked my castle for hours and you have not once asked why my portraits stop at eleven.
...What do you mean?
I kept your face. I kept it for ten years, in the one gallery I never let anyone clean. It is the only face I could not improve.
You are the Royal Asset. You are the boy who got out. You are {prince_full}, and you have been so very hard to find.
...That's not possible. I would remember.
Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years. I have only been looking after it. Surely you can see that.
Come. You may as well see it used properly.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.be: the Pathwork Throne
The castle does not fall. It opens. Where the Model Room floor was, a stair of four colours winds down into the old heart of the Capital.
At the bottom stands the Pathwork Throne: four seats grown into one, four colours woven as a single thread. It was never {villain}'s.
You sit, and the Throne answers. It knows you.
Everything comes back at once: the lullaby, the glass, the throne room, the name. {prince_full}. And the Paths, all four, as they were always meant to be carried.
{villain} Sees
{villain} sits among the pieces of his model. As the Paths settle, he sees the kingdom as it is, and not as his reflection.
Cracked streets. Real faces. A boy he kept in a cell.
Slowly, he understands how much he broke. The wells were good. The schools were good. He made one choice for everyone, and nobody will trust him with another.
File Complete
Agnes Overdue floats up to the old transfer file, finds the heir clause and, with great ceremony, brings down her stamp: HEIR: ALIVE. FILE COMPLETE.
You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.
'{prince},' she says. It is the first time anyone has said it aloud and meant it. 'Welcome home.'
data/story/capital_story.tres::freed_npc: Do not look so alarmed. The guard is very kind, and the workshop has a very nice window.
I am designing a water main. A real one: pipes, a pump and nothing clever. It is the first thing I have made in ten years that nobody had to agree to.
I am not permitted to speak of the Paths, or to touch one. I find that I do not miss it. I find that I miss the wells.
He is allowed visitors, one at a time, ten minutes, no mirrors. Those are the rules. I did not write them, and I find I do not mind them.
He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/hob: Ah. You did it, then. The castle.
Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in the city. Grave Row. Come by when you're ready. No rush. There never is, with me.
Back again! Walked them all the way home, I did. Lovely evening for it.
What are you writing?
Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/isl: Someone is walking down the imperial road in faded pastel regulation clothes, a bedroll over one shoulder. Brannoch has stopped writing in his notebook.
Hi, Dad. I know. I should have written.
Eight years. Gate stayed open. Every night. In case.
They had us painting the same front door for eight years. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending".
...You've got your mother's curls. Still can't keep a ribbon in them.
And your nose. Mum always said that was the unlucky part.
Wrote you in the book. Every day. "Isla. Not yet."
You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Thank you.
I keep walking to the gate and back. Nobody stops me. I keep expecting somebody to stop me.
Dad oiled the hinges this morning. It doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/roy: Grave Row, at dusk. At the end of the identical rows stand two new headstones, and they are not identical. Someone has carved them by hand: a crown, a harp, four colours in a ring.
Half the city has come. Nobody was told to. Wren holds the true record. Maren holds a pie she has forgotten about.
Ten years I've been digging these two. Slowly. I didn't want to finish before they could be visited properly.
Two forms, filed ten years ago, stamped by me. And a third, for a little boy, that I never had the heart to file.
I'm tearing that one up now, dear. With great pleasure.
He used to say the Paths argued like family. She used to say that was the point.
A warm wind comes up the row, out of season. Two figures stand by the headstones, the way people stand in a doorway when they are leaving and not sorry to.
Look at you. You came home.
Carry them gently, love. All four of them.
She hums the first bars of the lullaby, and does not need to finish it. You know the rest.
Right then, Your Majesties. Mind the step. It's a long one, but it's downhill all the way.
And you, Agnes. I've had you down for this a very long time.
One more week, Hob. Prudence needs a proper handover, and somebody has to explain the new handbook to Mortimer.
When you look again there are two headstones, a top hat bobbing away down the row, and a great deal of warm wind.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/bra: Notebook's full of her name. Started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled right, this time.
data/story/intro_story.tres::still.reuni: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.
Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.
At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
data/story/capital_story.tres::ending.po: With {villain} gone, the Paths are free to mix again. Your decks may now combine cards from ALL Paths, and the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is open. What made the kingdom strong was never sameness.
Decks may now use 3 or more Paths.
The Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is unlocked (no tri-Path recipes exist yet).
{pathordia} is open to everyone: the facade is down, the rifts are sealed, and {villain} works under guard on wells and pipes, kept away from every Path.
{villain} is gone, and the Paths are shouting at each other in the street again. I have never been so glad to be annoyed.
The Capital is open to everyone now, and your decks may mix any Paths you like. Go and see what you can make of it, dearie. Then come home and eat.
data/story/intro_story.tres::town.object: {villain} has fallen and the Paths are free to mix. Build decks from three or four Paths at once, try the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting, test yourself in the Undercroft and visit the changed Capital.
data/story/intro_story.tres::postgame.re: You came for me. Twice, if you count the woods. I'm counting the woods.
Finish it, Tess. I'll be here. I've had a lot of practice waiting in this forest.
The Lab is quiet. For the first time in ten years I can hear the trees from down there.
Dad is in {town}, listening to Maren. She let him have one slice of pie. One. I've never seen him so frightened.
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::T: The protein shake stand in the Swole Station
core/quests/zone_quest_definitions.gd::s: Old Man Mountain won't show you the way up Mount Swolympus on an empty cup. Bring him a protein shake from the Station's stand.
Buy a protein shake at the Station's stand
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::ques: Only the worthy reach the top. Also bring water.

There's a mountain behind the station... and a barbell on top older than the regime. Older than me, nearly. Bring me a protein shake from the stand and I'll show you the way. Can't climb on an empty cup.
Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Don't spill it. I spilled one, the Festival year... where was I.
That's the best water I've ever seen. Thank you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two was water.
Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... never gets enough credit for being there.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its hands out, palms up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years. It is very, very ready.
'Lift,' it rumbles. 'I will catch it. I have always caught it.'
data/encounters/boss_intros.json::The An: One more rep. There is always one more rep.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: One More Rep
At half health the Spotter catches the weight: it heals 4.
Lift. I will catch it. I have always caught it.
The Ancient Spotter heals 4.
Young Spotters
On its 6th turn two 1/1 Young Spotters climb up to help it.
Next turn: two Young Spotters climb up the mountain.
Never lift alone. Not even me.
Two 1/1 Young Spotters arrive.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.
'One more rep,' it says. Then, quieter: '...That was the one. Thank you for coming up.'
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/lab: The hatch opens on white light and a smell of disinfectant. A staircase of clean steel goes down through the roots of the forest where you woke up.
Everything about this place is familiar in the way a bruise is familiar. Your hands are shaking. You go down anyway.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: The Observation Deck
A gallery of glass above the cells, a kettle, a cracked mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST PATH-OLOGIST, and a corkboard of notes on one subject. The newest are a count of days.
Read the notes on the Subject
Drain cycles, power readings, a column labelled 'cooperative?' that someone has filled in with 'asks for his mother.' You put the notes down very carefully.
Drink the Path-ologists' tea
It is the first thing here that tastes like anything. You feel steadier.
Rifle the lockers
Keycards, a petty cash tin, and a half-written resignation letter.
data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::: Mutation
At half health the experiment sheds a piece of itself: a 1/1 Discarded Sample crawls out.
GRRRK. (The tag on its wrist reads: BATCH 12. DISCONTINUED.)
A 1/1 Discarded Sample crawls out.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::dung: Decontamination
Four nozzles hiss in four colors. A sensor asks whether your deck can carry more than one Path at a time.
The Draining Chamber
A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different color. This is where it was done.
Put your hand on the glass
The four colors lean toward your palm like plants toward a window. They were yours. They remember.
Read the dials
Every cycle logged, every reading neat. You learn exactly how the machine works, which is how to break it.
Tear out the straps
They come away easily. They were only ever as strong as the people who buckled them.
data/story/story_scenes.json::scenes/lab: A white room, three paces by four. Ten years of tally marks on the wall in rows of five, scratched with a spoon handle. Low down, where a child could reach, a drawing in four colors.
Someone is sitting under the drawing with her knees up and her hands bound, as if she has been keeping it company.
Took you long enough, Tess.
Tess?
That's what I called you, when we were small and you were too important to be called anything shorter.
They put me in your cell. My father thinks that's educational. With him it is hard to tell.
data/dungeons/dungeon_content.json::even: Your old cell: ten years of tally marks, a child's drawing in four colors, and Elowen under it with her hands bound.

Subject 1. And my daughter. Both of you home at once. I shall have to rearrange the schedule.
You have grown. Remarkable. The draining has been very good for your posture.
You held the door, Dad. The night they killed the King and Queen. I read it in your own hand.
I held a door, sweetheart. Doors are held every day. What came through it was the Minister's choice, not mine.
You told me he was a patient. I brought him soup. For years.
And it was very good soup. You were always confused about kindness. It made you a poor scientist and a lovely daughter.
Please, both of you, sit. This will only drain a little.
Tess. His Protocols run on switches, and I know where every one is. I'll take one down each turn. You do the rest.
